meta.note: Plain-language summaries of the terms each instrument defines. The cited paragraph governs.

MD-AA.def: NBFC notified under sub-clause (iii) of clause (f) of section 45-I of the Act that undertakes the account aggregator business, for a fee or otherwise, as defined in para 8(4).

Banking company; corresponding new bank; State Bank of India; subsidiary bank; any bank RBI notifies for these directions; or co-operative bank under clause (cci) of section 5 read with section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Same meaning as in clause (c) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

Under contract, retrieving or collecting customer financial information as RBI specifies, and consolidating, organising and presenting it to the customer or another financial information user as RBI specifies. Such information is not the AA's property and must not be used in any other manner.
Company registered under section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, or under sub-section (20) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013.
A person who has entered into a contractual arrangement with the Account Aggregator to avail its services.
Company granted a certificate of registration under sub-section (1A) of section 12 of the SEBI Act, 1992.
Person registered under sub-section (1A) of section 12 of the SEBI Act, 1992.

Information held with financial information providers on: bank and NBFC deposits; structured investment products; CP; CDs; tradable G-Secs; equity shares, bonds, debentures; MF, ETF, CIS and AIF units; IDRs; insurance policies; NPS balances; InvIT and REIT units; GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B returns; and any other RBI-specified information.
For these directions: RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, and Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

Bank, banking company, NBFC, asset management company, depository, depository participant, insurance company, insurance repository, Central Recordkeeping Agency, GSTN, Clearing Corporation of India Ltd, or other RBI-identified entity. CCIL provides G-Sec holdings in Retail Direct Gilt accounts.
Entity registered with and regulated by any financial sector regulator.
Company formed under the Companies Act, 1956, granted IRDAI registration to maintain electronic insurance policy data for insurers.
Outside liabilities excluding borrowings or loans from group entities, divided by Owned Funds.
Company registered under the Companies Act and granted an RBI certificate of registration under section 45IA of the Act.
(i) individual; (ii) Hindu undivided family; (iii) company; (iv) firm; (v) association of persons or body of individuals, incorporated or not; (vi) any other artificial juridical person.

MD-ACQ.def: Same meaning as in clause (e) of sub-regulation (1) of regulation 2 of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies- Acceptance of Public Deposits) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in clause 77 of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013.
A jurisdiction whose name does not appear in either FATF publication: (i) High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action; or (ii) Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring.

Meaning as defined in the applicable accounting standards. A new investor from or through FATF non-compliant jurisdictions may not directly or indirectly acquire it; fresh such investors in aggregate must be less than 20 per cent of voting power (including potential voting power).

Voting power that could arise from convertible instruments, other instruments with (including contingent) voting rights, or contractual arrangements granting future voting rights. New FATF non-compliant investment must be below both 20 per cent of existing voting power and 20 per cent of existing plus potential voting power.

MD-ALM.def: Time taken to liquidate an investment position, based on its liquidity in the secondary market.
Risk that changes in market interest rates might adversely affect the NBFC's financial condition.
Customers exercising options for premature closure of deposits and prepayment of loans and advances.

Measurement of mismatches between rate-sensitive liabilities and rate-sensitive assets, including off-balance sheet positions, through a Gap Report that groups them into time buckets by residual maturity or next repricing period, whichever is earlier.
Liabilities and general obligations collateralised by legal rights to specifically designated assets owned by the borrowing institution.
Evaluation of a regulated entity's (RE's) financial position under a severe but plausible scenario, to assist decision-making within the RE.
Free of legal, regulatory, contractual or other restrictions on the NBFC's ability to liquidate, sell, transfer or assign an asset.
NBFC's capacity to fund asset increases and meet expected and unexpected cash and collateral obligations at reasonable cost and without unacceptable losses.

Inability of an NBFC to meet obligations as they fall due without adversely affecting its financial condition. Effective management helps ensure obligations are met when due and reduces the probability of an adverse situation developing.

MD-AMLG.def: The entity proposed to transfer its business to another entity under a scheme of amalgamation.
The entity which is to acquire the business of the amalgamated entity under a scheme of amalgamation.

One or more entities merging with another entity under relevant statutes or regulations under a scheme of amalgamation (or whatever name called), which sets out the terms and modalities of the process.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (NBFCs – Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Guidelines, 2025, as amended from time to time.
The National Company Law Tribunal constituted under section 408 of the Companies Act, 2013 (as defined in sub-section (90) of section 2 of that Act), as amended from time to time.

MD-AUDREP.def: A company as defined in section 45-I(f) of the RBI Act, 1934, other than companies RBI has exempted under section 45NC from the applicability of section 45-IA. The Directions apply to auditors of such NBFCs.

Defined in the RBI (NBFC - Acceptance of Public Deposits) Directions, 2025, which this page does not reproduce. Para 7(1) counts it with unsecured NCDs/bonds from the public and shareholder borrowings (public limited companies), excluding items excluded from that definition.

MD-AUTH.def: Process of validating and confirming the credentials of the customer who originates the payment instruction.
Transaction where the card and acceptance infrastructure are not present in close proximity while making the transaction.
Transaction carried out through the physical use of a card at the point of transaction.
Payment instruction in which a card issued by an Indian issuer is used to pay a merchant acquired by an overseas acquirer. Involves outflow of foreign exchange.
Same meaning as in Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 ('Electronic Funds Transfer').

Customer credential used for authentication, from 'something the user has', 'something the user knows' or 'something the user is'. May include password, SMS-based OTP, passphrase, PIN, card hardware, software token, fingerprint or other biometrics (device-native or Aadhaar-based).
Bank or non-bank that maintains the customer's account from which payment is made, such as a deposit account, credit line or prepaid instrument.

MD-AUTH.term: Words and expressions not defined in these Directions
MD-AUTH.def: Same meaning as in Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

MD-AUTH.term: tokenisation, token requestor, use cases/channels, token storage mechanisms
MD-AUTH.def: Same meaning as in RBI directions on 'Tokenisation - Card Transactions' dated January 08, 2019, as amended from time to time.

MD-CAP.def: Clearing house interposing itself between counterparties, becoming buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer, and so ensuring future performance of open contracts. It becomes counterparty via novation, an open offer system or other legally binding arrangement. For capital purposes, a CCP is a financial institution.

Arrangement of two or more entities related through: subsidiary-parent, joint venture, associate, or promoter-promotee (per SEBI Takeover Regulations, 1997, for listed companies); related party; common brand name; or equity investment of 20% or more. Parent, subsidiary, joint venture, associate and related party are as defined in Accounting Standards.

Amount payable by the credit protection seller to the buyer under a credit derivative after a credit event. Payment is only by physical settlement (par against physical delivery of a deliverable obligation).

In bilateral netting, the larger of zero or the market value of a transaction or netting-set portfolio with a counterparty that would be lost if the counterparty defaults, assuming no recovery in bankruptcy. Also called Replacement Cost (RC).
Any obligation of the reference entity that must be delivered under the contract if a credit event occurs. It ranks at least pari passu with, or junior to, the underlying obligation.
A capital instrument with characteristics of both equity and debt.
Total outside liabilities divided by owned fund.

MD-CAP.term: NBFC primarily engaged in lending against gold jewellery
MD-CAP.def: An NBFC in which loans against gold jewellery comprise 50 percent or more of its financial assets.

Group of transactions with a single counterparty that are subject to a legally enforceable bilateral netting arrangement recognised for capital purposes. Each transaction not under such an arrangement is its own netting set.

A CCP licensed to operate (including by confirmed exemption) and permitted by its regulator to operate for the products offered, based and prudentially supervised in a jurisdiction with domestic rules consistent with CPSS-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures.
Obligation used to calculate the amount payable when a credit event occurs under a credit derivative. Relevant for obligations cash-settled on a par-less-recovery basis.

Instrument that is fully paid up, unsecured, subordinated to other creditors' claims, free from restrictive clauses, and not redeemable at the holder's instance or without the supervisory authority's consent.

Contractually defined segment of an exposure's or pool's credit risk, where a position carries more or less credit-loss risk than an equal position in another segment, ignoring third-party credit protection held directly by segment holders. Securitisation notes issued by the SPE and credit enhancement facilities count as tranches.
The tranche's effective maturity in years, measured as prescribed in paragraphs 38 to 40.
Detachment point (D) minus attachment point (A), with D and A calculated under paragraphs 33 to 37.
The asset which a protection buyer is seeking to hedge.
Terms bear the meanings given in the RBI NBFC Securitisation Transactions Directions, 2025, unless stated otherwise in these Directions.

Paid-up equity capital, compulsorily convertible preference shares, free reserves, share premium, and asset-sale capital reserves (excluding revaluation reserves), less accumulated losses, intangible assets and deferred revenue expenditure. Quarterly profits count only if limited-reviewed or audited quarterly, net of 3-year average dividend (EPt = NPt - 0.25xDxt); current-year losses are fully deducted.

MD-CARDS.def: Supplementary card to a principal or primary credit card, issued to persons with a predefined relationship to the primary cardholder, within the primary card's credit limits and liability, on terms the card-issuer stipulates.
Annual cost of credit to the cardholder, including interest and all other charges under different scenarios based on card features.
Regular length of time between closing dates of two consecutive bills raised by the card-issuer.
Cards issued to business entities or individuals for business expenses under specified terms; not for personal use.
A person to whom a card is issued, or who is authorised to use an issued card.
An NBFC permitted by RBI to issue credit cards in India.
Schemes linked to a card under which the issuer or associated merchants offer digital coupons, points, discounts, cash backs or other monetary-value benefits, redeemable after accumulation.
A credit card where the full billed amount must be paid on the due date after the billing cycle; no rollover of credit to the next billing cycle is permitted.
A card jointly issued by a card-issuer and a co-branding entity, bearing the names of both partners.
A fixed or pro-rata charge on credit card use as an alternative payment form not ordinarily accepted compared with other payment forms.
A credit card issued to specific employees of a corporate employer; liability may rest with the corporate, the employee, or both, per product design.
A physical or virtual payment instrument with a means of identification, issued with a pre-approved revolving credit limit, usable to buy goods or services or draw cash advances, on prescribed terms.
The maximum revolving credit determined and notified to the cardholder to transact in the credit card account.
A physical or virtual instrument usable in place of a card to undertake a payment or banking transaction.
Period from transaction date to payment due date in which interest-free payment can be made, provided the entire outstanding is paid on or before the due date.
Minimum part of the total bill a cardholder must pay so as not to be treated as an overdue bill.
Standard conditions for issuing and using credit cards, defining the responsibilities and liabilities of the card-issuer and cardholder.
Same meaning as Prepaid Payment Instrument in the Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments dated August 27, 2021.
The customer issued a credit card by a card-issuer, in whose name the card account is opened.
Total amount payable as per the credit card statement generated at the end of a billing cycle, net of any credit received during that cycle.

Credit card issued without a specific written or digital request or application. Renewal or replacement cards are not unsolicited; replacement covers account-relationship changes, technology upgrades, or reissue of lost, blocked or suspended cards, but not a new account opened after closure.
Enhancement in the benefits and features of an issued credit card, for example an increase in its credit or cash limit.

MD-CDS.def: Settlement process in which the price of the reference or deliverable obligation, at which settlement happens, is determined through an auction mechanism.
Settlement process in which the protection seller pays the protection buyer the CDS notional amount less the expected recovery value of the reference obligation.
Entity interposed between counterparties to contracts traded in financial markets, becoming buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer, thereby ensuring performance of open contracts.
Same meaning as in s.2(20) of the Companies Act, 2013.

Non-convertible debt securities that create or acknowledge indebtedness, including debentures, bonds and similar securities issued by a body corporate, trust or statutory body, whether or not charged on issuer's assets. Excludes money market debt instruments, security receipts, securitised debt, and bonds issued by Central or State Government or persons RBI specifies.

Credit derivative in which the protection seller agrees to pay the protection buyer on a credit event for a reference entity, and the buyer pays periodic premium until contract maturity or the credit event, whichever is earlier.
Derivative contract whose value is derived from the credit risk of an underlying debt instrument or of an index of underlying debt instruments.
Pre-defined event in a credit derivative contract that triggers settlement under the contract.
Debt instrument issued by the reference entity that the protection buyer can deliver to the protection seller in a physically settled CDS after a credit event.
Same meaning as in para 2(iii) of the RBI Electronic Trading Platforms Directions, 2025 dated January 16, 2025, as amended from time to time.
Means 'recognised stock exchange', with the same meaning as in s.2(f) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.
Standardised derivative traded on a recognised stock exchange to buy or sell an index of debt instruments at a specified future date, at a price determined when the contract is made.
Same meaning as in para 9 of Ind AS 24: Related Party Disclosures.
Undertaking a credit derivative transaction to reduce the credit risk of a particular debt instrument or of a portfolio of debt instruments.

Company engaged primarily in activities related to infrastructure sub-sectors in the Harmonized Master List of Infrastructure Sub-sectors (DEA gazette notification F.No.13/6/2009-INF dated April 08, 2016), as amended.
Entity that provides prices to users and other market-makers.

Commercial papers and non-convertible debentures of original or initial maturity up to one year (as defined in the CP and NCD Directions, 2024 dated January 03, 2024), and certificates of deposit (as defined in the CD Directions, 2021 dated June 04, 2021), as amended.
Same meaning as in s.2(57) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Markets where transactions are undertaken in any manner other than on exchanges, including electronic trading platforms.
Same meaning as in s.2(w) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
Settlement process in which the protection buyer delivers any eligible deliverable obligation to the protection seller against receipt of the CDS notional amount.
Debt instrument issued by a reference entity, or an index of debt instruments, specified in a total return swap contract.
Entity against whose credit risk a credit derivative contract is entered into.
Debt instrument issued by the reference entity and specified in a CDS contract, used for valuation, for the cash settlement value, or as the deliverable obligation on a credit event.
Same meaning as in para 9 of Ind AS 24: Related Party Disclosures.
Means 'person resident in India', with the same meaning as in s.2(v) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
CDS contract in which the underlying is a single reference entity.
Any event that results in the reference obligation being replaced by another obligation issued by the reference entity.
Any event that results in the reference entity no longer being the primary obligor for the reference obligation.

Credit derivative in which the total return payer transfers the entire economic performance of a reference asset to the total return receiver and, in return, receives a pre-determined fixed or floating rate linked to a benchmark.
Person that undertakes derivative transactions other than as a market-maker.

Replacement of a market-maker with another market-maker in an OTC derivative contract: the transferor steps out, and a new contract forms between the remaining party and the transferee, who becomes the new counterparty.
MD-CDS.scope: Does not apply to novation by a central counterparty for settlement, or under RBI circular DBOD.No.BP.BC.76/21.04.157/2013-14 dated December 09, 2013

MD-CDS.def: In novation, the user, market-maker or central counterparty that continues as counterparty in the new contract after novation.
Same meaning as in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (the Act) or in the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.

MD-CIC.def: NBFC acquiring shares that, on last audited balance sheet, has: (1) at least 90% of net assets in group-company equity, preference shares, bonds, debentures, debt or loans; (2) at least 60% of net assets in group equity (incl. compulsorily convertible within 10 years) and InvIT sponsor units; (3) no trading except block sales for dilution or disinvestment; (4) no other financial activity beyond listed exceptions.

Owned funds per last audited balance sheet, plus 50% of unrealised appreciation in quoted investments and any equity capital increase since then; less capital contributions by one CIC in another exceeding 10% of the investing CIC's owned funds, diminution in book value of quoted investments, and any equity capital reduction since then.
Equity capital and reserves less intangible assets and revaluation reserves, divided by the investee's number of equity shares.
Book value of assets plus interest accrued but not received.

Entities linked by subsidiary-parent (AS 21), joint venture (AS 27), associate (AS 23), promoter-promotee (SEBI Takeover Regulations, listed companies), related party (AS 18), common brand name, or equity investment of 20% or more.
RBI directions issued from time to time on Fair Practices Code and Know Your Customer guidelines.
Same meaning as in clause (e) of sub-regulation (1) of regulation 2 of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.
Core investment company with total assets of at least Rs 100 crore, individually or in aggregate with other CICs in its group, that raises or holds public funds.
Investment readily realisable by nature and intended to be held for not more than one year from the date it is made.
Interaction between the CIC and its customers while carrying on its business.

Average post-tax profit of the preceding three years, less preference dividend and adjusted for extraordinary and non-recurring items, divided by investee's equity shares, capitalised at 8% (predominantly manufacturing), 10% (predominantly trading) or 12% (any other company, including NBFC). Loss-making investee: zero.
Mean of earning value and break-up value.
Capital instrument with characteristics of both equity and debt.
Shares, stock, bonds, debentures or securities issued by Government or a local authority, or other marketable securities of a like nature.
Trust registered under SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, as amended from time to time.
Any investment other than a current investment.
Average of weekly highs and lows of closing price on the exchange where most actively traded, over the 26 weeks immediately preceding the financial year-end of the last audited balance sheet.
Total assets excluding (i) cash and bank balances, (ii) money market instruments and money market mutual funds, (iii) advance payments of taxes, and (iv) deferred tax payment.
Latest declared net asset value by the mutual fund for that particular scheme.

(i) Hire purchase asset: overdue and future instalments receivable, less unmatured finance charges, less provisions under para 35. (ii) Leased asset: capital portion of overdue lease rentals receivable plus depreciated book value, adjusted by lease adjustment account balance.

Total balance-sheet liabilities excluding paid-up capital, reserves and surplus, and instruments compulsorily convertible into equity within 10 years of issue; includes all debt-like obligations and guarantees issued, whether on balance sheet or not.

Paid-up equity, compulsorily convertible preference shares, free reserves incl. quarterly profits, share premium, and asset-sale capital reserves; excludes revaluation reserves. Less accumulated losses, intangibles, deferred revenue expenditure. Quarterly profits count only with quarterly limited review/audit, net of 0.25 x average three-year dividend. Current-year losses fully deducted. No ROU asset deduction if the leased asset is tangible.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Acceptance of Public Deposits) Directions, 2025.

Funds raised directly or indirectly through public deposits, inter-corporate deposits, bank finance, and all outside-source funds such as commercial papers and debentures; excludes instruments compulsorily convertible into equity within 10 years of issue.

Beneficial interest held by an individual, spouse or minor child, singly or together, in a company's shares exceeding 10% of its paid-up capital; or capital subscribed by all partners of a partnership firm.
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act 2 of 1934).
Total of all assets appearing on the assets side of the balance sheet.

CIC with asset size under Rs 100 crore (whether or not accessing public funds), or Rs 100 crore or more and not accessing public funds; need not register under section 45IA of the RBI Act. Must be able to meet any group guarantees without recourse to public funds.

MD-CIR.def: Same meaning as in section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, or the corresponding section of the Companies Act, 2013.

Companies granted a certificate of registration under section 5 of CICRA. Registered CICs: CRIF Credit Information Services Private Limited (November 25, 2010); Equifax Credit Information Services Private Limited (March 26, 2010); Experian Credit Information Company of India Private Limited (February 17, 2010); TransUnion CIBIL Limited (March 05, 2012).
Same meaning as in section 2(l) of CICRA, and those notified under regulation 3 of the Credit Information Companies Regulations, 2006, as amended.

MD-CLIMATE.def: Activities or projects meeting the requirements prescribed in para 13.
Interest-bearing deposit received by an NBFC for a fixed period, the proceeds of which are earmarked for allocation towards green finance.

Lending to and/or investing in green activities/projects meeting para 13 requirements. Contributes to climate risk mitigation, climate adaptation and resilience, and other climate or environmental objectives, including biodiversity management and nature-based solutions.
Marketing products or services as green when they do not meet the requirements to be defined as green activities/projects.

MD-CLIMATE.term: Eligible green activities / projects - interim categories
MD-CLIMATE.def: Interim measure pending the official Indian green taxonomy. Categories: renewable energy (solar, wind, biomass or hydropower projects integrating generation and storage); energy efficiency; clean transportation (including EV charging infrastructure); climate change adaptation; sustainable water and waste management; pollution prevention and control; green buildings; sustainable living natural resources and land use; terrestrial and aquatic biodiversity conservation.
MD-CLIMATE.scope: Interim, pending finalisation of the official Indian green taxonomy

MD-CLIMATE.term: Exclusions from eligible green activities / projects
MD-CLIMATE.def: Fossil-fuel extraction, production, distribution or upgrades, or projects whose core energy source is fossil-fuel based; nuclear power generation; direct waste incineration; alcohol, weapons, tobacco, gaming or palm oil industries; biomass energy from protected-area feedstock; landfill projects; hydropower plants larger than 25 MW.

MD-COMPL.def: NBFCs in the Middle Layer and Upper Layer, holding registration under the RBI Act 1934 or Factoring Regulation Act 2011, collectively 'NBFCs'.
MD-COMPL.scope: Middle Layer and Upper Layer NBFCs only; unless specified otherwise

MD-COMPL.def: Risk of legal or regulatory sanctions, material financial loss, or loss to reputation that an NBFC may suffer from failing to comply with laws, regulations, rules and codes of conduct applicable to its activities.

MD-CONC.def: Right to appoint a majority of directors, or to control management or policy decisions, alone or in concert, directly or indirectly (via shareholding, management rights, shareholder or voting agreements, or otherwise). Same as Clause (27) of Section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Tier 1 capital as defined at paragraph 4(8).

Two or more persons where: (i) one controls the other, or both are under common control of a third party (automatic if one owns over 50% of the other's voting rights); or (ii) economic interdependence per criteria (a)-(h), e.g. 50%+ of gross receipts or expenditure from the other. Identify such links where exposure to one counterparty exceeds 5% of eligible capital base.

Credit facility to a borrower by term loan, project loan, subscription to bonds, debentures, preference or equity shares of a project company (acquired in a project finance package, in the nature of advance), or other long-term funded facility, for infrastructure sub-sectors notified by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance.

Infrastructure lending to projects meeting all six criteria: one year of operations after commercial operations date without material covenant breach; standard asset; revenue from concession or contract rights protected for the full term; escrow, pari passu charge and early-termination safeguards for lenders; sufficient funding; no further encumbrance without existing lenders' consent.

Sum of all exposure values of an NBFC-UL, measured per paragraph 41, to a counterparty and/or group of connected counterparties, if equal to or above 10 per cent of the NBFC-UL's eligible capital base.

Non-deposit taking NBFC referred to in the RBI NOFHC Directions, 2025, which holds shares of a banking company and of all other financial services companies in its group, to the extent permissible under applicable prescriptions.
Same meaning as in Chapter II of the RBI (NBFC - Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025.

Same meaning as in Chapter II of the RBI (NBFC - Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025. For concentration norms, the NBFC must obtain an external auditor's certificate on completing capital augmentation and submit it to the Department of Supervision before reckoning the additions.
MD-CONC.scope: Concentration norms only (for the auditor certificate condition)

MD-CONC.def: Same meaning as in the RBI NOFHC Directions, 2025.
As defined in paragraph 10 of the RBI (NBFC - Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025.

MD-CPNCD.def: Export Import Bank of India; National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development; National Housing Bank; Small Industries Development Bank of India; and National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development.

Banking company (including Payment Bank and Small Finance Bank) under s.5(c) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; or a 'regional rural bank', 'corresponding new bank' or 'State Bank of India' (ss.5(ja), (da), (nc)); or a 'cooperative bank' under s.5(cci) read with s.56 of that Act.
Any entity incorporated by or under any Statute in force. Excludes co-operative societies registered under co-operative society law.
Unsecured money market instrument issued in the form of a promissory note.
Same meaning as in s.2(20) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Same meaning as in s.5(cciia) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, read with s.56.
Settlement mechanism in which transfer of funds from the securities buyer is made simultaneously with transfer of securities by the seller.
Same meaning as in s.2(e) of the Depositories Act, 1996.
Entity registered with SEBI as debenture trustee under the SEBI (Debenture Trustees) Regulations, 1993.
Same meaning as in para 2(iii) of the RBI Electronic Trading Platforms Directions, 2018 dated October 05, 2018, as modified from time to time.

Person who controls the creation, operation and administration of financial benchmark(s) authorised under the RBI Financial Benchmark Administrators Directions, 2023 dated December 28, 2023, as amended.

Two or more entities related through: (a) subsidiary-parent (Ind-AS 110/AS 21); (b) joint venture (Ind-AS 28/AS 27); (c) associate (Ind-AS 28/AS 23); (d) promoter-promotee (SEBI Takeover Regulations, 1997) for listed companies; (e) common brand name; or (f) investment in equity shares of 20 per cent and above.
Business trust as defined in sub-clause (i) of clause 13A of s.2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
Scheduled Commercial Bank undertaking the duties and responsibilities specified under para 7(a) of these Directions.
Same meaning as in s.2(n) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.
Same meaning as in s.45U(b) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
A company as defined in s.45I(f) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Secured money market instrument with an original or initial maturity up to one year.
Same meaning as 'person resident outside India' in s.2(w) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
Markets where transactions are undertaken in any manner other than on recognised stock exchanges, including those undertaken on electronic trading platforms.
Same meaning as in s.2(69) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Business trust as defined in sub-clause (ii) of clause 13A of s.2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
Same meaning as in s.2(f) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.
Same meaning as under Ind AS 24 or IAS 24 (Related Party Disclosures), or any other equivalent accounting standard.
Same meaning as 'person resident in India' in s.2(v) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
Same meaning as in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

MD-CREDIT.def: The date on which the project is put to commercial use, with a completion or provisional completion certificate.
As defined in the Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025.
The date defined in the concession agreement between the concessionaire and the concession authority.
MD-CREDIT.scope: Infrastructure projects under the PPP model

MD-CREDIT.def: Loans where both principal and interest fall due at maturity.
An existing asset of the borrower pledged to the lender to secure a credit facility.
Any permissible loan that is not an income generating loan.
Triggered on events listed in the paragraph, starting with a default with any lender.
A contractual arrangement, by whatever name, under which another entity covers loss due to default up to an agreed share of the NBFC's loan portfolio.
A remote and automated lending process, largely using seamless digital technologies for customer acquisition, credit assessment, approval, disbursement, recovery and servicing.
Mobile or web-based applications, standalone or part of a suite, that provide digital lending services.
The date on which the project's capital structure is tied up, accounting for at least 90 per cent of total project cost.
Non-payment of debt (as defined in the IBC, 2016) when the whole or any part of it has become due and is not paid.
The revised DCCO, if the original DCCO is revised.
Financing for purchase, construction, reconstruction, renovation or repair of residential dwelling units, including the items listed in the paragraph.
Loans for productive economic activities, such as farm credit and loans for business.
The sub-sectors in the Government's Harmonised Master List of Infrastructure sub-sectors.
Interest accrued on a lender's debt and capitalised during the project's construction phase.
Items designed to be worn as personal adornments.
An agent of the NBFC (including another lender) that carries out one or more of its digital lending functions.
The date, envisaged at financial closure, by which the project is expected to be put to commercial use.
Items used to adorn objects, decorative items or utensils, excluding the items the paragraph lists.
Gold and silver in any form other than jewellery, ornaments and coins.

Ventures undertaken through capital expenditure for creating or expanding tangible assets or facilities expected to yield cash flows far into the future, usually with a long gestation period, irreversibility and substantial capital outlay.

Funding a project in which the revenues the funded project will generate are the primary security. It covers greenfield and brownfield financing. An exposure counts as project finance only if (a) at least 51 per cent of the predominant repayment source, as envisaged at financial closure, is the project's own cash flows, and (b) all lenders have a common agreement with the debtor. Loan terms may differ between lenders, except the original, extended or actual DCCO (para 68), if the debtor and all lenders agree.
As defined in the Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025.
An additional loan sanctioned over and above an outstanding loan during the original loan's tenor.
Same meaning as in section 2(e) of the CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023.

MD-CRM.def: Bilateral derivative on one or more reference assets: the protection buyer pays a fee over the contract's life, and the protection seller makes a credit event payment after a credit event of the reference entities.

MD-CRM.term: Committee on lending to related parties
MD-CRM.def: Board committee entrusted with sanctioning loans to related parties. NBFCs may designate an existing committee for this, other than the Audit Committee.
Same meaning as in Section 188(1)(a) to (g) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Same meaning as in Section 2(27) of the Companies Act, 2013.

Amount the protection seller pays the protection buyer after a credit event under the credit derivative. Payment is only by physical settlement: payment of par against physical delivery of a deliverable obligation.

Any obligation of the reference entity, as defined in the RBI Credit Derivatives Directions, 2022, that must be delivered under the contract if a credit event occurs. It must rank at least pari passu with, or junior to, the underlying obligation.

MD-CRM.term: Director of an NBFC or any other entity
MD-CRM.def: A director appointed or elected to the Board of the entity.
A person other than an individual or a Hindu Undivided Family.
Same meaning as in Section 2(51) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Extending funded and/or non-fund-based credit facilities to related parties. Investments in their debt instruments are covered; equity investments are excluded.
Person holding 10 per cent or more of paid-up share capital, or Rs 5 crore in paid-up shares, whichever is less.
Same meaning as in Section 3(23) of Part I of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016.
Same meaning as in Banking Statistics (Harmonised Definitions), except that for these Directions it excludes loans for investments in financial assets.
Same meaning as in Section 2(69) of the Companies Act, 2013.

Obligation, as defined in the RBI Credit Derivatives Directions, 2022, used to calculate the amount payable when a credit event occurs. Relevant for obligations cash-settled on a par-less-recovery basis.

Related person, or entity where related person is partner, manager, KMP, director or promoter; holds over 10% equity; controls; can nominate a director; controls over 20% voting rights; accustomed to act on its advice; guarantor or surety; private-trust trustee, author or beneficiary; or subsidiary, parent, holding, associate or JV. Excludes lending-only nominations, professional advice, and common govt ownership.

A person and that person's relatives, where the person is a promoter, director or KMP of the NBFC; owns over 5% of paid-up equity or can exercise over 5% of voting rights; can nominate a director by agreement with the NBFC; or controls the NBFC alone or jointly.
Same meaning as in Clause (77) of Section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013 and rules framed under it.
All employees positioned up to two levels below the Board, and any employee designated as such under the NBFC's policy.
The asset or obligation which a protection buyer is seeking to hedge.
NBFC-Factors, NBFC-D, and non-deposit taking NBFCs with asset size of Rs 500 crore and above.

MD-CYBER.def: NBFCs registered with RBI under the RBI Act 1934, Factoring Regulation Act 2011 or NHB Act 1987, collectively 'NBFCs'.

Chronological record that reconstructs and examines the sequence of activities surrounding or leading to a specific operation, procedure or event in a security-relevant transaction, from inception to result.
Property of being accessible and usable on demand by an authorised entity.
Property that information is neither made available nor disclosed to unauthorised individuals, entities, processes or systems.
Relating to, within, or through the medium of the interconnected information infrastructure of interactions among persons, processes, data and information systems.
Any observable occurrence in an information system. Cyber events sometimes indicate that a cyber incident is occurring.

Preservation of confidentiality, integrity and availability of information and/or information systems through the cyber medium. Authenticity, accountability, non-repudiation and reliability may also be involved.
A cyber event that adversely affects the cybersecurity of an information asset, whether resulting from malicious activity or not. Includes both cybersecurity incidents and IT incidents.

Ability of an organisation to continue its mission by anticipating and adapting to cyber threats and environmental changes, and by withstanding, containing and rapidly recovering from cyber incidents.
Malicious attempt(s) to exploit vulnerabilities through the cyber medium to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorised access to assets.
A circumstance with the potential to exploit one or more vulnerabilities that adversely affects cybersecurity.
Description of data in business terms, including data types, structure details and security restrictions.
Perimeter network segment logically located between internal and external networks.
A denial of service carried out using numerous sources simultaneously.
Process used to acquire, preserve, analyse and report on evidence using scientific methods that are demonstrably reliable, accurate and repeatable.
Structured set of strategies, policies, procedures, methods and best practices that guides organisational activities, enables governance and supports achievement of defined objectives.
Any piece of data, device or other component of the environment that supports information-related activities. Includes information system, data, hardware and software.
Set of applications, services, information technology assets or other information-handling components, including the operating environment and networks.
Property of accuracy and completeness.
Leadership, organisational structures and processes, under executives and the board, that ensure the enterprise's IT sustains and extends its strategies and objectives.
Business risk associated with the use, ownership, operation, involvement, influence and adoption of IT within an enterprise.
Software designed with malicious intent, with features or capabilities that can potentially cause direct or indirect harm to entities or their information systems.
Test methodology in which assessors, typically working under specific constraints, attempt to circumvent or defeat the security features of an information system.
Digital social engineering that attempts to acquire private or confidential information by pretending to be a trustworthy entity in electronic communication.
User who, by function and/or role, has powers within an information system significantly greater than those available to most users.
The point in time to which data must be recovered after an outage.
Overall length of time an information system's components can be in the recovery phase before negatively impacting the organisation's mission or business processes.
A weakness, susceptibility or flaw of an asset or control that can be exploited by one or more threats.

Systematic examination of an information system or product to determine adequacy of security measures, identify deficiencies, predict effectiveness of proposed measures, and confirm adequacy after implementation.
Refers to 'digital forensics' for the purpose of these Directions.
In these Directions, 'incident' implies a cyber incident.
MD-CYBER.scope: Unless specified otherwise in the Directions

MD-DEP.def: Any person who has made a deposit with a company, or the heir, legal representative, administrator or assignee of such depositor.
A Housing Finance Company granted RBI registration to accept public deposits.
An NBFC granted RBI registration to accept public deposits.

Aggregate of share premium balance, capital and debenture redemption reserves, and any other balance-sheet reserve created by allocating profits. Excludes reserves for future liabilities, depreciation or bad debts, and reserves created by asset revaluation.
Same meaning as in the RBI NBFC Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy Directions, 2025.
A company registered under section 3 of the Insurance Act, 1938.
Same meaning as 'NBFC-ICC' in the RBI NBFC Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation Directions, 2025.

Any of: (i) public financial institution under s.4A of the Companies Act, 1956; (ii) State Financial, Industrial or Investment Corporation; (iii) scheduled commercial bank; (iv) General Insurance Corporation of India (s.9, GIB Act 1972); (v) institution RBI specifies by notification.
A company notified as a financial institution by the Central Government under section 620A of the Companies Act, 1956.

Company not notified under s.620A of the Companies Act, 1956 that carried on non-banking financial business on 9 January 1997, has net owned funds plus preferential share capital of at least Rs 10 lakh, applied for registration by 9 July 1997, and complies with Nidhi-company directions under s.637A.
Same meaning as NOF in section 45-IA of the RBI Act, 1934, including paid-up preference shares compulsorily convertible into equity.
Only an investment and credit company, HFC, mutual benefit financial company, or factor registered under s.3 of the Factoring Regulation Act, 2011.
MD-DEP.scope: Applies only for the purposes of these Directions

MD-DEP.def: NBFC that: (i) fails within five working days to meet a lawful demand to repay matured public deposits; (ii) reports default to a small depositor to CLB/NCLT under s.58AA; (iii) seeks withdrawal of liquid asset securities for deposit obligations; (iv) seeks RBI relief or exemption to avoid default; or (v) is identified by RBI as problem NBFC.
Deposit as defined in section 45-I(bb) of the RBI Act, 1934, excluding the items in sub-paragraphs (i) to (xv), each listed separately below.
Amounts from the Central or State Government, or from any source whose repayment they guarantee; from a local authority, foreign Government, or any foreign citizen, authority or person.

Amounts from named bodies (e.g. IDBI, LIC, GIC and its subsidiaries, SIDBI, Unit Trust of India, NABARD, electricity boards, ADB, IFC, and listed development corporations), a company under the Companies Act, 1956, a statutory corporation, a registered cooperative society, or institutions RBI specifies.
Amounts received by a company from any other company.

Share application money or advances towards allotment received under a Companies Act, 2013 securities offer, to the extent and for the period permitted by the Companies (Acceptance of Deposit) Rules, 2014.

Amounts from a director when paying, or from shareholders of a private company (including a former private company under s.43A, 1956 Act) whose articles retain s.3(1)(iii) provisions. Requires written declaration that money is not borrowed. Joint shareholders other than the first named are not treated as shareholders.

Amounts from bonds or debentures secured by mortgage of immovable property or other assets, or compulsorily convertible into equity. For secured bonds or debentures, the amount must not exceed the market value of the property or assets.
Amounts from non-convertible debentures with maturity over one year and minimum subscription of Rs 1 crore or more per investor, issued under RBI guidelines in force.

Unsecured loans brought in by promoters under lending institution stipulations, if: (a) the loan fulfils the institution's promoter-contribution stipulation; (b) it comes from the promoters and/or their relatives, not friends or business associates; (c) the exemption lasts only until the institution's loan is repaid.
Amounts from a mutual fund governed by the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.
Hybrid debt or subordinated debt with minimum maturity of sixty months or more, provided the issuer has no recall option within that period.
Amounts from a relative of a director of the NBFC, accepted only on an application stating the depositor is related to that director as a relative under the Companies Act, 1956 or 2013.
Amounts received by issuing commercial paper under the RBI Master Direction on Commercial Paper and NCDs of original maturity up to one year, 2024.
Amounts received by an NBFC-Middle Layer or above (except deposit-taking NBFCs) through perpetual debt instruments issued under RBI guidelines.
Amounts from infrastructure bonds issued by an Infrastructure Finance Company, as notified by the Central Government under section 80CCF of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
Amounts an HFC receives from the NHB or any Public Housing Agency.
Same meaning as in section 2(h) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.
Same meaning and treatment as in the RBI NBFC Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy Directions, 2025.
A company doing business as a stock-broker or sub-broker and holding a valid registration under section 12 of the SEBI Act, 1992.
A company recognised as a stock exchange under section 4 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.
Aggregate public deposits of up to Rs 10,000 standing in the sole or first-named depositor's name in the same capacity across all branches of the NBFC.

MD-DIV.def: Adjusted Net Worth, calculated under the applicable prudential norms on capital adequacy.
Capital to Risk Weighted Assets Ratio, calculated under the applicable prudential norms on capital adequacy.
Dividend payable in a year (including interim dividend) divided by the net profit for the year per audited financial statements for the financial year for which dividend is proposed.
Same meaning as in applicable Accounting Standards.
Ratio of NNPA to net advances.

MD-DPSC.def: Credit-card issuing NBFCs, collectively 'NBFCs' and individually 'NBFC'.
Property of being accessible and usable on demand by an authorised entity.
Property that information is neither made available nor disclosed to unauthorised individuals, entities, processes or systems.
Relating to, within, or through the medium of the interconnected information infrastructure of interactions among persons, processes, data and information systems.

Preservation of confidentiality, integrity and availability of information and/or information systems through the cyber medium. Authenticity, accountability, non-repudiation and reliability may also be involved.
Malicious attempt(s) to exploit vulnerabilities through the cyber medium to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorised access to assets.
A denial of service carried out using numerous sources simultaneously.
Structured set of strategies, policies, procedures, methods and best practices that guides organisational activities, enables governance and supports achievement of defined objectives.
Set of applications, services, information technology assets or other information-handling components, including the operating environment and networks.
Software designed with malicious intent, with features or capabilities that can potentially cause direct or indirect harm to entities or their information systems.
Test methodology in which assessors, typically working under specific constraints, attempt to circumvent or defeat the security features of an information system.
Digital social engineering that attempts to acquire private or confidential information by pretending to be a trustworthy entity in electronic communication.
A weakness, susceptibility or flaw of an asset or control that can be exploited by one or more threats.

Systematic examination of an information system or product to determine adequacy of security measures, identify deficiencies, predict effectiveness of proposed measures, and confirm adequacy after implementation.

MD-EMANDATE.def: Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 and Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA).
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 and Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA).
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 and Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA).
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 and Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA).

MD-FEMA-ECB.def: Credits extended by an overseas supplier, bank, financial institution or other permitted recognised lender, for the maturity prescribed in this framework, for imports of capital or non-capital goods permissible under the Foreign Trade Policy. Includes suppliers' credit and buyers' credit depending on source of finance.

Rate of interest, other fees, expenses, charges, guarantee fees and ECA charges, in FC or INR, excluding commitment fees and INR withholding tax. Fixed-rate loans: swap cost plus spread must not exceed floating rate plus applicable spread. FCCB issue expenses max 4% of issue size (2% for private placement). Components must be paid without using ECB/TC drawdown proceeds.
MD-FEMA-ECB.scope: Para 1 marked Deleted on page; text quoted in footnote 4

MD-FEMA-ECB.def: ECB/TC may be raised under the automatic route or the approval route. Under the approval route, prospective borrowers send requests to RBI through their AD Banks for examination.
MD-FEMA-ECB.scope: Para 1 marked Deleted on page; text quoted in footnote 4

MD-FEMA-ECB.def: Same meaning as in FEMA, 1999, s.10(1).
MD-FEMA-ECB.scope: Para 1 marked Deleted on page; text quoted in footnote 4

MD-FEMA-ECB.def: Cases under the automatic route are examined by AD Category-I banks.
MD-FEMA-ECB.scope: Para 1 marked Deleted on page; text quoted in footnote 4

MD-FEMA-ECB.def: For FCY ECB/TC: any widely accepted interbank rate, or ARR, of 6-month tenor applicable to the borrowing currency. For Rupee-denominated ECB/TC: prevailing yield of Government of India securities of corresponding maturity.
MD-FEMA-ECB.scope: Para 1 marked Deleted on page; text quoted in footnote 4

MD-FEMA-ECB.term: Designated Authorised Dealer Category I Bank
MD-FEMA-ECB.def: Bank branch designated by the ECB/TC borrower to meet reporting requirements (including obtaining the LRN/LIN from RBI), exercise delegated powers under these guidelines, and monitor ECB/TC transactions.
MD-FEMA-ECB.scope: Para 1 marked Deleted on page; text quoted in footnote 4

MD-FEMA-FDI.def: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (42 of 1999).
Equity shares, convertible debentures, preference shares and share warrants issued by an Indian company (details in para 4).

A company under the Companies Act, 2013, or a body corporate set up under a Central or State Act, incorporated in India. Excludes societies, trusts and entities excluded as eligible investees under the FDI Policy. A company qualified as a Companies Act 2013 company covers only such companies.
Same meaning as in the Companies Act, 2013. For an LLP, the right to appoint a majority of designated partners who, with specific exclusion of others, control all LLP policies.

Instrument issued by a start-up company, initially recorded as debt, repayable at the holder's option or convertible into equity shares within not more than ten years from issue, on specified events under agreed terms.
Buying and selling of goods and services, including digital products, over digital and electronic networks.

Entity conducting e-commerce that is (1) a company under the Companies Act 1956 or 2013; (2) a foreign company under s. 2(42) of the Companies Act 2013; or (3) an office, branch or agency in India owned or controlled by a non-resident.
E-commerce where the e-commerce entity owns the inventory of goods and services and sells them directly to consumers. Foreign investment is not permitted in this model (para 2.6.4).
E-commerce where the e-commerce entity provides an IT platform on a digital and electronic network to act as facilitator between buyer and seller.
Sector-specific conditions in Schedule I of the NDI Rules for companies receiving foreign investment.

Investment through equity instruments by a non-resident in (a) an unlisted Indian company, or (b) 10% or more of post-issue paid-up equity capital, fully diluted, of a listed Indian company. A listed-company holding that later falls below 10% continues as FDI.
Total shares that would be outstanding if all possible sources of conversion were exercised.

Non-resident investment in equity instruments that is (a) less than 10% of post-issue paid-up equity capital, fully diluted, of a listed Indian company, or (b) less than 10% of paid-up value of each series of equity instruments of a listed Indian company.

Person registered under the SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations, 2014. A registered FII or sub-account with a valid SEBI certificate is deemed an FPI until the three-year block from the enactment of the 2014 Regulations expires.
Investment by a non-resident on a repatriable basis in equity instruments of an Indian company or in capital of an LLP. A non-resident may hold foreign investment as FDI or as FPI.
Issue or transfer of participating interest or rights in oil fields by Indian companies to a non-resident is treated as foreign investment.
Where a declaration under the Companies Act 2013 shows a non-resident beneficial interest, the holding is counted as foreign investment, even if made by a resident Indian citizen.
Two or more enterprises where one can, directly or indirectly, exercise 26% or more of voting rights in the other, or appoint more than 50% of the other's board of directors.
An Indian company or an LLP.

Subscribing, acquiring, holding or transferring any security or unit issued by a person resident in India, including depository receipts issued abroad whose underlying is such a security. For an LLP, capital contribution or acquisition or transfer of profit shares.
'Employees' stock option' as defined under the Companies Act, 2013 and issued under SEBI regulations.
Sweat equity shares as defined under the Companies Act, 2013.

Issue of equity instruments to non-resident employees or directors of the holding company, joint venture, or wholly owned overseas subsidiary or subsidiaries, under share-based employee benefit schemes of an Indian company.
Investment whose sale or maturity proceeds, net of taxes, are eligible for repatriation. 'Investment on non-repatriation basis' is construed accordingly.

Entity registered and regulated under SEBI or another designated authority's regulations: REITs (SEBI REIT Regulations 2014), InvITs (SEBI InvIT Regulations 2014), and AIFs (SEBI AIF Regulations 2012).
A VCF registered under the SEBI (Venture Capital Fund) Regulations, 1996, whether a trust, company or body corporate, is not an Investment Vehicle for the NDI Rules and this Master Direction.
Partnership formed and registered under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.
Indian company with any equity instrument listed on a recognised stock exchange in India. 'Unlisted Indian Company' is construed accordingly.

Instruments per S.O. 3722(E) dated October 16, 2019: equity in incorporated entities; LLP capital; FDI-policy instruments; units of AIFs, REITs and InvITs; MF or ETF units investing over 50% in equity; equity tranche of securitisation; direct dealing in immovable property; contribution to trusts; depository receipts against equity.
Individual resident outside India who is a citizen of India.
Individual resident outside India registered as an Overseas Citizen of India cardholder under s. 7(A) of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
Individual resident in India who is a citizen of India under the Constitution or the Citizenship Act, 1955.

Dealing in land and immovable property for profit. Excludes townships, residential or commercial premises, roads or bridges, educational institutions, recreational facilities, and city or regional infrastructure; REIT units; rent on leases not amounting to transfer; and real estate broking (100% automatic route).

Includes sale, exchange or relinquishment of the asset; extinguishment of rights; compulsory acquisition; allowing possession in part performance under s. 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882; or acquiring capital instruments that transfer or enable enjoyment of immovable property.

Maximum investment, including foreign investment on repatriation basis in equity of a company or LLP capital, and indirect foreign investment, unless provided otherwise. A composite limit for the investee Indian entity.

FCCBs and DRs whose underlying instruments are debt in nature are excluded from the sectoral cap (2.27.1). Equity arising from conversion of any debt instrument under any arrangement is counted toward it (2.27.2).

Beneficial interest of an investor in an investment vehicle, including partly paid units permitted under SEBI regulations. AIF partly paid units issued before the 2024 Second Amendment Rules need compounding under FEMA.
Includes any rupee vostro accounts, including Special Rupee Vostro Accounts, that a non-resident may hold under Regulation 7(1) of the FEM (Deposit) Regulations, 2016.
Same meaning as in the Act, the Rules, and the Regulations made thereunder.
Approval from the erstwhile SIA/DIPP and/or FIPB and/or any Government ministry or department. Applications are made on the DPIIT Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal (FIFP).
Shares issued under the Companies Act, 2013, including partly paid equity shares.

Partly paid shares issued on or after July 8, 2014 are equity instruments. For non-residents, 25% of total consideration (incl. premium) is received upfront, and the balance within 12 months, with full call within 12 months. Monitoring-agency exceptions apply (4.3.3, 4.3.4).

Warrants issued under SEBI regulations, the Companies Act 2013 or other law, on or after July 8, 2014, are equity instruments. Pricing and conversion formula are fixed upfront; at least 25% is received upfront and the balance within 18 months.
Fully and mandatorily convertible debentures that are fully paid. Debentures not fully, compulsorily and mandatorily convertible are debt instruments outside the NDI Rules (para 4.6.2).
Fully and mandatorily convertible preference shares that are fully paid. Other preference shares are debt instruments outside the NDI Rules (para 4.7.2).

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: beneficial owner of an investment into India
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: Beneficial owner of the investor entity incorporated or registered in a country other than a land-border country.
Same meaning as in s. 2(1)(fa) of the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002, determined per rule 9(3) of the PMLA (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: beneficial ownership vested in a land-border country
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: Deemed vested where a citizen or entity of such a country can, alone or jointly, (A) hold rights above PMLA Rule 9(3) thresholds over a non-land-border investor entity, (B) control that investor entity, or (C) exercise ultimate effective control over the investee.
Same meaning as in para 9.1.1 of these directions.
Same meaning as in the Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022, as amended.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: fair price of capital contribution/profit share of an LLP
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: Investment in an LLP must not be less than the fair price under an internationally accepted valuation norm, certified by a Chartered Accountant, a practicing Cost Accountant, or an approved valuer on the Central Government panel.

FPIs, including foreign Governments or their related entities, with common ownership (direct or indirect) of more than 50% or common control form an investor group. For Annex 2 it has the meaning in the SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019.
Beneficial holding of more than 50% of the equity instruments of the company.
Contribution of more than 50% of its capital, with a majority profit share.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: Company owned by resident Indian citizens
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: Indian company whose ownership is vested in resident Indian citizens and/or Indian companies ultimately owned and controlled by them.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: LLP owned by resident Indian citizens
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: LLP whose ownership is vested in resident Indian citizens and/or Indian entities ultimately owned and controlled by them.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: Company owned by persons resident outside India
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: Indian company whose ownership is vested in persons resident outside India.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: LLP owned by persons resident outside India
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: LLP whose ownership is vested in persons resident outside India.
Right to appoint a majority of directors, or to control management or policy decisions, including through shareholding, management rights, shareholders' agreement or voting agreement.
Right to appoint a majority of designated partners who, with specific exclusion of others, control all LLP policies.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: Company controlled by resident Indian citizens
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: Indian company whose control is vested in resident Indian citizens and/or Indian companies ultimately owned and controlled by them.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: LLP controlled by resident Indian citizens
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: LLP whose control is vested in resident Indian citizens and/or Indian entities ultimately owned and controlled by them.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: Company controlled by persons resident outside India
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: Indian company whose control is vested in persons resident outside India.

MD-FEMA-FDI.term: LLP controlled by persons resident outside India
MD-FEMA-FDI.def: LLP whose control is vested in persons resident outside India.
Investment by an Indian entity that has received foreign investment, or by an Investment Vehicle, in the equity instruments or capital of another Indian entity.
Same meaning as in the Companies Act, 2013.

Downstream investment received by an Indian entity from (1) an Indian entity that received foreign investment and is not resident-Indian-owned and controlled, or is owned or controlled by non-residents; or (2) an investment vehicle whose sponsor, manager or investment manager is not resident-Indian-owned and controlled, or is non-resident owned or controlled (SEBI decides for other forms).

Where the investor entity later becomes owned and/or controlled by non-residents, the investment is downstream from that date. It must comply with the entry route and sectoral cap and be reported by the investor entity in Form DI within 30 days.

NRI/OCI non-repatriation investments are deemed domestic. An Indian entity owned and controlled by NRIs/OCIs, investing on a non-repatriation basis under Schedule IV, is not counted in indirect foreign investment.
Sum of foreign investment and indirect foreign investment, calculated on a fully diluted basis.
Downstream investment by banking companies incorporated in India in their subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates.

MD-FEMA-ODI.def: Entity formed, registered or incorporated outside India (including in an IFSC in India) with limited liability (e.g., LLC, LLP), where the liability of the Indian resident is clear and limited. For a regulated investment fund set up as a trust abroad, the Indian resident's liability must not exceed its interest or contribution, and the trustee must be a non-resident.

Includes energy and natural resources sectors (oil, gas, coal, mineral ores), submarine cable systems and start-ups, plus any sector or sub-sector the Central Government deems fit. Limited-liability structure is not mandatory for foreign entities whose core activity is in a strategic sector, so unincorporated entities are allowed. Remittances need any required competent-authority permission.

Right to appoint a majority of directors or to control management or policy decisions, alone or in concert, directly or indirectly, through shareholding, management rights, shareholders' or voting agreements entitling the holder to 10% or more of voting rights, or otherwise.

A company under the Companies Act, 2013, a body corporate incorporated under any law, a Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008, or a partnership firm registered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. Each investor entity is separately considered an Indian entity.

Entity of a foreign entity in which the foreign entity has control. It must meet the foreign-entity structure requirements, including limited liability, unless the foreign entity's core activity is in a strategic sector. Investees where the foreign entity lacks control are not SDS and need not be reported.

(i) Acquiring unlisted equity capital or subscribing as part of the Memorandum of Association of a foreign entity; (ii) investing 10% or more of paid-up equity of a listed foreign entity; or (iii) investing with control where below 10% of a listed foreign entity's paid-up equity. An investment stays ODI even if it falls below 10% or control is lost.

Equity shares, perpetual capital, irredeemable instruments, or contribution to non-debt capital of a foreign entity, being fully and compulsorily convertible instruments. Redeemable, non-convertible or optionally convertible instruments are treated as debt.

Aggregate of ODI, debt other than Overseas Portfolio Investment, and non-fund-based facilities extended by a resident to all foreign entities. An Indian entity may lend or invest in a foreign entity's debt, or give non-fund commitments (including to overseas SDSs), only if it is eligible for ODI, has made ODI in that foreign entity, and acquired control on or before the commitment.

Investment other than ODI in foreign securities. Not permitted in: unlisted debt instruments; securities issued by a resident not in an IFSC; derivatives unless RBI permits; or commodities including Bullion Depository Receipts. OPI in a listed equity that is later delisted stays OPI until further investment, which must then be ODI.
OPI proceeds are exempt from repatriation provisions as long as they are reinvested within the realisation and repatriation time under FEMA Notification 9(R)/2015-RB.
Also includes funds whose activities are regulated by the host jurisdiction's financial sector regulator through a fund manager.

Where the OI Rules, OI Regulations or these Directions refer to listed equity capital or a listed instrument overseas, it means equity or an instrument listed on a recognised stock exchange outside India.

MD-FINSVC.def: Any company to which the NBFC currently has, or previously had, a loan or investment exposure (excluding equity instruments) at any time during the preceding twelve months.
Equity shares, compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) and compulsorily convertible debentures (CCD).

Company engaged in business of financial services, including business under Banking Regulation Act 1949 s6(1)(a),(c),(d),(e) as notified under s6(1)(o); RBI Act s45I(c),(f); credit information; payment systems; stock, commodity or derivatives exchanges; depositories; asset reconstruction; SEBI intermediaries; credit rating; collective investment schemes; pension fund management; FEMA authorised persons; other business RBI specifies.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (NBFCs – Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Guidelines, 2025.
Same meaning as in the Accounting Standards of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.
Same meaning as in SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.
Company engaged in businesses other than those specified in para 4(3).
Same meaning as in the Accounting Standards of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.

MD-FRAUD.def: Date when due approval from the competent authority is obtained for the classification and the reasoned order is passed.
Actual date the fraud came to light in the concerned branch, audit or department of the Applicable NBFC. Not the date of competent-authority approval.
Date the actual misappropriation of funds started, or the event occurred, as evidenced or reported in audit or other findings.

NBFCs registered under the RBI Act or Factoring Regulation Act, and HFCs registered under the NHB Act where applicable, in the Upper Layer, Middle Layer, and Base Layer with asset size of ₹500 crore and above. Asset size is per audited balance sheet as on 31 March of the preceding financial year.
Same meaning as in Section 45I(f) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
In this context, 'Board' means the Board of Directors of the Applicable NBFC.
Domestic and overseas subsidiaries, affiliates and joint ventures, as defined under applicable accounting standards, whether engaged in financial or non-financial services.

An entity is associated if another entity is its subsidiary (Companies Act 2013, cl. 2(87)), or a joint venture or associate company (s. 2(6)). For a natural person, all entities where the person is promoter, director, or in charge of management are associated.

MD-FS.def: Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Sum of the LTVs of loans at the time of sanction, divided by the total number of such loans.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.

Date from which the cited Credit Facilities Directions apply to NFB facilities: April 1, 2026, or any earlier date an NBFC adopts under its internal policy. NFB facilities extended or renewed before that date remain under existing bank instructions.

Date from which the cited Transfer and Distribution of Credit Risk Directions apply to co-lending arrangements: January 1, 2026, or any earlier date an NBFC adopts under its internal policy. Any new CLA after that date must comply.

MD-GOV.def: Contractual agreement under which an employee agrees to return previously paid or vested remuneration to the regulated entity in certain circumstances.
A company registered under Section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, or the corresponding provision of the Companies Act, 2013.
A director appointed on the Board of an NBFC.
Same meaning as in Section 149(6) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Same meaning as in clause 51 of Section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013.
An arrangement allowing an NBFC to prevent vesting of all or part of a deferred remuneration. It does not reverse vesting once vesting has already occurred.
Same meaning as in clause 77 of Section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013.
The period after vesting of instruments awarded as variable pay during which they cannot be sold or accessed.
Same meaning as in the 'Explanation' to Section 178 of the Companies Act, 2013.

Holding of a beneficial interest, alone or together with spouse or minor child, in a company's shares whose paid-up amount exceeds 10% of the company's paid-up capital; or, for a partnership firm, the capital subscribed by all its partners.

MD-HFC.def: Book value of assets plus interest accrued on them but not yet received.
Company registered under section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, or the corresponding provision of the Companies Act, 2013.

Two or more entities linked by: subsidiary-parent (AS 21), joint venture (AS 27), associate (AS 23), promoter-promotee (SEBI Takeover Regulations 1997, listed companies), related party (AS 18), common brand name, or equity investment of 20% or more.
Investment readily realisable by nature and intended to be held for not more than one year from the date it is made.

Average post-tax profit of the preceding three years, less preference dividend and adjusted for extraordinary and non-recurring items, divided by the investee's equity shares and capitalised at 8% (predominantly manufacturing), 10% (predominantly trading) or 12% (any other company, including NBFC/HFC). Loss-making investee: zero.
Arithmetic mean of earning value and breakup value.

Aggregate of share premium, capital and debenture redemption reserves and other balance-sheet reserves created by profit allocation; excludes reserves for future liabilities, depreciation or bad debts, and revaluation reserves.

Finance for buying, building, reconstructing, renovating or repairing residential dwellings, under categories (i)-(xi) (e.g., individual dwelling loans, plot loans with build declaration within three years, builder and public agency loans, employee housing). Furnishing and other non-housing loans excluded. Commercial space up to 10% of project FSI in integrated housing counts as residential.

Company under Companies Act, 2013 that is an NBFC where (i) housing finance is at least 60% of total assets (net of intangibles), and (ii) at least 50% of total assets (net of intangibles) is individual housing finance under 10(8)(i)-(v). Notes: NBFC status if financial assets exceed 50% of total assets and financial income exceeds 50% of gross income.
Capital instrument with characteristics of both equity and debt.
Latest declared net asset value of the relevant mutual fund scheme.

(i) Hire purchase asset: overdue and future instalments receivable, less unmatured finance charges, less provisions under para 49. (ii) Leased asset: capital portion of overdue lease rentals receivable plus depreciated book value, adjusted by the lease adjustment account balance.
Net owned fund as defined in section 29A of the National Housing Bank Act, 1987, including paid-up preference shares compulsorily convertible into equity.
National Housing Bank established under section 3 of the National Housing Bank Act, 1987.
National Housing Bank Act, 1987 (Act 53 of 1987).

Paid-up equity, compulsorily convertible preference shares, free reserves incl. quarterly profits, share premium, and asset-sale capital reserves; excludes revaluation reserves. Less accumulated losses, intangibles, deferred revenue expenditure. Quarterly profits count only with quarterly limited review/audit, net of 0.25 x average three-year dividend. Current-year losses fully deducted. No ROU asset deduction if the leased asset is tangible.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Acceptance of Public Deposits) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025; capital treatment also per those Directions.

Owned fund less investments in shares of other NBFCs/HFCs, and in shares, debentures, bonds, loans, advances (incl. hire purchase and lease finance) and deposits with subsidiaries and same-group companies, where that aggregate exceeds 10% of owned fund.

(i) Preference shares other than compulsorily convertible ones; (ii) revaluation reserves at 55% discounted rate; (iii) general provisions and loss reserves not attributable to identified diminution, up to 1.25% of risk-weighted assets; (iv) hybrid debt instruments meeting Annex I; (v) subordinated debt. Total not to exceed Tier 1 capital.

MD-IA.term: Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) and Housing Finance Companies (HFCs)
MD-IA.def: NBFCs holding RBI registration under the RBI Act, 1934 or Factoring Regulation Act, 2011, and HFCs holding registration under the National Housing Bank Act, 1987. Covers all deposit-taking NBFCs and HFCs, and non-deposit-taking NBFCs and HFCs with asset size of Rs 5,000 crore and above.
MD-IA.scope: Non-deposit-taking NBFCs and HFCs below Rs 5,000 crore asset size are excluded

MD-IA.def: The Risk-Based Internal Audit framework, as the third line of defence, intended to strengthen the effectiveness of Internal Audit systems and processes in NBFCs.
Evaluation of the effectiveness of control systems for monitoring the inherent risks of business activities. Risk assessment draws a risk matrix combining inherent business risks and control risks.

MD-INV.def: Book value of the assets plus interest accrued on them but not received.
Investment which is by nature readily realisable and intended to be held for not more than one year from the date it is made.
Any investment other than a current investment.
