Same meaning as in SEBI circular SEBI/HO/AFD-1/PoD/P/CIR/2022/157 dated November 23, 2022.
Any company to which the NBFC currently has, or previously had at any time in the preceding 12 months, a loan or investment exposure.
References to investment in subordinated units of an AIF scheme include all forms of subordinated exposure, including investment in the nature of sponsor units.

MD-IO.def: Executive Director, Managing Director or Chief Executive Officer in the NBFC.
A representation in writing or through other modes alleging deficiency in service on the part of the NBFC, with or without seeking relief.
A company as defined in the Companies Act, 2013 that has been granted a certificate of registration under section 5(2) of the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005.
A person who uses, or is an applicant for, a service provided by the NBFC.
A shortcoming or inadequacy in any service the NBFC is required to provide, statutorily or otherwise, which may or may not result in financial loss or damage to the customer.
Any person appointed under clause 6 of these Directions.
Regulatory body for financial sector entities, including RBI (RBI Act, 1934), SEBI (SEBI Act, 1992), IRDAI (IRDAI Act, 1999) and PFRDA (PFRDA Act, 2013).
Any person appointed under clause 5 of these Directions.

A commercial bank, payments bank, small finance bank, NBFC, non-bank prepaid payment instrument issuer or credit information company covered by the Internal Ombudsman framework, or any other entity RBI may specify.

MD-IO.term: Words or expressions not defined herein
MD-IO.def: Same meaning as in the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, RBI Act, 1934, Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005, CIC Rules, 2006, CIC Regulations, 2006, or the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, or RBI regulations, directions and guidelines.

MD-IRACP.def: Either (i) an asset identified as loss by the NBFC, its internal or external auditor, or RBI during inspection, to the extent not written off; or (ii) an asset adversely affected by a potential threat of non-recoverability from eroded or unavailable security, or a fraudulent act or omission by the borrower.
Any amount due to an NBFC under any credit facility is overdue if not paid on the due date fixed by the NBFC.
Asset with no perceived default in repayment of principal or payment of interest, which shows no problem and carries no more than normal risk attached to the business.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in RBI circular FIDD.MSME & NFS.BC.No.3/06.02.31/2020-21 dated July 2, 2020 on credit flow to MSMEs, as updated from time to time.
Same meaning as in RBI circular FIDD.MSME & NFS.BC.No.3/06.02.31/2020-21 dated July 2, 2020 on credit flow to MSMEs, as updated from time to time.
Same meaning as in RBI circular FIDD.MSME & NFS.BC.No.3/06.02.31/2020-21 dated July 2, 2020 on credit flow to MSMEs, as updated from time to time.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.

MD-IRACP.term: Commercial Real Estate – Residential Housing Sector (CRE - RH)
MD-IRACP.def: Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.

MD-IRD.def: Arrangement under which an overseas entity (including overseas branches, IFSC Banking Units, wholly owned subsidiaries or joint ventures of market-makers) transacts with a non-resident and immediately enters an off-setting transaction with the India market-maker. For foreign banks, this may be through any branch of the parent bank.
Interest rate administered by a Financial Benchmark Administrator.
Same meaning as in s.2(20) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Same meaning as in para 2(a)(ii) of the RBI Electronic Trading Platforms Directions, 2025 dated June 16, 2025, as amended.

MD-IRD.term: European Interest Rate Call / Put Option
MD-IRD.def: Interest rate call or put option contract that can be exercised only on its expiration date.

Person who controls the creation, operation and administration of financial benchmark(s) authorised under the RBI Financial Benchmark Administrators Directions, 2023 dated December 28, 2023, as amended.

MD-IRD.term: Foreign Currency Settled Interest Rate Derivative (FCS-IRD)
MD-IRD.def: Rupee interest rate derivative contract whose settlement currency is a currency other than the Indian Rupee.
Person registered under the SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations, 2019, as amended.

Cash-settled OTC contract in which, on the settlement date, the buyer pays or receives the difference between a pre-determined fixed FRA rate and a predetermined floating rate, price or index, applied on a notional principal for a specified forward period.

Interest rate option giving the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an interest rate instrument, or receive or pay an interest rate on a notional principal, at a pre-determined price or rate on or before a specified expiration date.
Series of interest rate call options (caplets) in which the buyer receives a payment at the end of each period when the underlying interest rate is above the agreed strike rate.
Derivative in which a market participant simultaneously buys an interest rate cap and sells an interest rate floor on the same rate, maturity and notional principal amount.
Series of interest rate put options in which the buyer receives a payment at the end of each period when the underlying interest rate is below the strike rate.

Standardised contract traded on a recognised stock exchange to buy or sell a notional security, interest-bearing instrument, index of such instruments or interest rates at a specified future date, at a price fixed at contract. Includes Money Market Futures.
Derivative contract involving exchange of a stream of agreed interest payments on a notional principal amount over a specified period.
Option on an interest rate swap giving the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to enter into that swap.
Same meaning as in s.2(f) of the Government Securities Act, 2006.
Undertaking a derivative transaction to reduce Rupee interest rate risk at balance sheet level, portfolio level, or individual asset or liability level.
Financial derivative contract whose value is derived from one or more Rupee interest rates, prices of Rupee interest rate instruments, or Rupee interest rate indices.

OTC derivative whose potential pay-out during the contract can exceed its notional amount, or whose pay-out involves multiplying the notional amount or underlying rate, price or index by a factor of more than 1.0.
Entity that provides prices to users and other market-makers. Market-makers need not have an underlying risk.
Interest rate future based on any Rupee-denominated money market interest rate or money market instrument.
Same meaning as in s.2(57) of the Companies Act, 2013, as amended.
Includes a 'person resident outside India' as defined in s.2(w) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
Market where derivative transactions are undertaken in any manner other than on exchanges, including on electronic trading platforms.
Same meaning as in s.2(f) of the Securities Contract Regulation Act, 1956.
Same meaning as in para 9 of Ind AS 24 or IAS 24, or any other equivalent accounting standard, but excluding associates as specified in those standards.
Includes a 'person resident in India' as defined in s.2(v) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
Derivative in which a market participant simultaneously buys an interest rate floor and sells an interest rate cap on the same rate, maturity and notional principal amount.
Same meaning as in s.2(91) of the Companies Act, 2013, as amended.
Person who undertakes derivative transactions other than as a market-maker.

Replacement of a market-maker with another market-maker in an OTC derivative contract: the transferor steps out, and a new contract forms between the remaining party and the transferee, who becomes the new counterparty.
MD-IRD.scope: Does not apply to novation by a central counterparty for settlement, or under RBI circular DBOD.No.BP.BC.76/21.04.157/2013-14 dated December 09, 2013

MD-IRD.def: In novation, the user, market-maker or central counterparty that continues as a counterparty in the new contract after novation.
Same meaning as in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (the Act) or in the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
Same meaning as in the RBI Market-makers in OTC Derivatives Directions, 2021 dated September 16, 2021, as amended.

Cap of ₹1,000 crore on the Price Value of a Basis Point (PVBP) of all outstanding IRD positions, including FCS-IRD positions, of non-residents. PVBP is computed by gross addition of each non-resident's PVBP, ignoring mathematical signs.
MD-IRD.scope: Applies only to non-resident IRD transactions for purposes other than hedging

MD-KYC.def: Same meaning as in clause (a) of section 2 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.
'Act' means the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 and 'Rules' the Prevention of Money-Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005, respectively, including amendments.
In the Aadhaar context, the process defined in sub-section (c) of section 2 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.

Natural person(s) who, alone, jointly or through juridical persons, have a controlling ownership interest or exercise control through other means. Controlling ownership interest means more than 10 percent of shares, capital or profits. Control includes the right to appoint a majority of directors or control management or policy decisions, via shareholding, management rights or shareholder/voting agreements.

Natural person(s) who, alone, jointly or through juridical persons, own or are entitled to more than 10 percent of capital or profits, or exercise control through other means. Control includes the right to control management or policy decisions.

MD-KYC.term: Beneficial Owner (BO) - unincorporated association or body of individuals (includes societies)
MD-KYC.def: Natural person(s) who, alone, jointly or through juridical persons, own or are entitled to more than 15 percent of property, capital or profits, or exercise control through other means. If no natural person is identified under (a), (b) or (c), the beneficial owner is the relevant natural person holding the position of senior managing official.

Identification must include the author of the trust, the trustee, beneficiaries with 10 percent or more interest in the trust, and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control through a chain of control or ownership.

Copy of the Aadhaar proof of possession (where offline verification cannot be carried out) or the officially valid document, compared with the original by an authorised officer of the NBFC, who records the comparison on the copy as per the Act.

MD-KYC.term: Certified Copy - alternative for NRIs and PIOs
MD-KYC.def: For NRIs and PIOs (as defined in FEMA 5(R)), an original certified copy may alternatively be certified by: an authorised official of an overseas branch of an Indian scheduled commercial bank; an overseas bank branch with which Indian banks have relationships; a notary public abroad; a court magistrate; a judge; or the Indian Embassy/Consulate General where the customer resides.
Entity defined under Rule 2(1) of the Rules that receives, stores, safeguards and retrieves customers' KYC records in digital form.

Person the NBFC designates to ensure overall compliance with obligations under Chapter IV of the PML Act and the Rules. Includes the Managing Director or a whole-time Director duly authorised by the Board; these terms have Companies Act, 2013 meanings.

An authorised officer of the NBFC captures a live photo of the customer and the officially valid document or Aadhaar proof of possession (where offline verification cannot be carried out), with the latitude and longitude of where the photo is taken, per the PML Act provisions.
Same meaning as in clause (p) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

Electronic equivalent of a document that its issuing authority issues with a valid digital signature, including documents issued to the customer's digital locker account under rule 9 of the Information Technology (Preservation and Retention of Information by Intermediaries Providing Digital Locker Facilities) Rules, 2016.
Same meaning as in clause (e) of sub-section (9) of section 286 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
Unique number or code the CKYCR assigns to a customer. Once generated and given to the NBFC, the NBFC shares it with the customer, who can also access it on the CKYCR portal.

Entity constituted for religious or charitable purposes under clause (15) of section 2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and registered as a trust or society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (or similar State law), or as a company under section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.

Passport; driving licence; proof of possession of Aadhaar number (may be in the form UIDAI issues); Voter's Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of India; NREGA job card duly signed by a State Government officer; and the letter issued by the National Population Register containing name and address.

MD-KYC.term: OVD - deemed OVD for limited proof of address
MD-KYC.def: Where an OVD lacks an updated address, these (or their equivalent e-documents) are deemed OVDs for proof of address only: utility bill not more than two months old (electricity, telephone, post-paid mobile, piped gas, water); property or municipal tax receipt; pension or family pension payment orders showing address; employer's allotment letter or leave-and-licence agreement for official accommodation.
Customer must submit an OVD with current address within three months of submitting the deemed OVD documents under para 5(1)(xiv)(b).

MD-KYC.term: OVD - foreign national without address details
MD-KYC.def: If a foreign national's OVD lacks address details, the NBFC accepts documents issued by government departments of foreign jurisdictions, and a letter from the Foreign Embassy or Mission in India, as proof of address.
A document is treated as an OVD even if the name changed after issuance, provided it is supported by a State Government marriage certificate or a Gazette notification indicating the change of name.
Same meaning as in clause (pa) of section 2 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.

Has the meaning in the Act and includes: an individual; a Hindu undivided family; a company; an association of persons or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not; every artificial juridical person not covered above; and any agency, office or branch owned or controlled by any of these.
NBFC's nominated officer at management level, responsible for furnishing information under rule 8 of the Rules.

A transaction (as defined), including an attempted one, whether or not in cash, which to a person acting in good faith: (a) gives reasonable ground to suspect proceeds of a PMLA Schedule offence, regardless of value; (b) appears unusually or unjustifiably complex; (c) has no economic rationale or bona fide purpose; or (d) gives reasonable ground to suspect terrorism financing.

Purchase, sale, loan, pledge, gift, transfer, delivery or arrangement of these. Includes: opening an account; deposit, withdrawal, exchange or transfer of funds in any currency by any means; use of a safe deposit box; entering a fiduciary relationship; any payment made or received for a contractual or legal obligation; establishing a legal person or legal arrangement.
Reporting standards for the multilateral agreement on automatic exchange of information, based on Article 6 of the Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters.
Person engaged in a financial transaction or activity with an NBFC, including a person on whose behalf that person is acting.
Person with no account-based relationship with the NBFC who undertakes transactions with it.
Identifying and verifying the customer and beneficial owner using reliable and independent sources of identification.

Applies at account commencement, for occasional transactions of Rs 50,000 or more (single or connected), and for any international money transfer. Includes: (a) identification, verification and purpose/intended nature of relationship; (b) understanding the customer's business, ownership and control; (c) determining whether the customer acts for a beneficial owner and verifying that owner.
Undertaking the CDD process.

US Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act, which among other things requires foreign financial institutions to report financial accounts held by US taxpayers or foreign entities in which US taxpayers hold a substantial ownership interest.
Inter Governmental Agreement between India and the USA to improve international tax compliance and implement FATCA.
Templates prepared to collate and report KYC data to the CKYCR, for individuals and legal entities.
Customers who open accounts without visiting the NBFC's branch or offices or meeting its officials.
Regular monitoring of transactions to ensure they are consistent with the NBFC's knowledge of the customer, business, risk profile and source of funds/wealth.
Steps to keep CDD documents, data or information up to date and relevant, by reviewing existing records at the periodicity prescribed by RBI.

(a) Banks: SCBs, RRBs, LABs, primary UCBs, StCBs/CCBs and any entity licensed under section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; (b) AIFIs; (c) NBFCs, MNBCs and RNBCs; (d) ARCs; (e) payment system providers/participants and PPI issuers; (f) authorised persons, including MTSS agents.

Bank with no physical presence in the country where it is incorporated and licensed, and unaffiliated with a regulated financial group subject to effective consolidated supervision. A local agent or low-level staff does not constitute physical presence.

Alternative identification method in which an authorised NBFC official conducts facial-recognition identification and CDD through a seamless, secure, live, consent-based audio-visual interaction, with independent verification and an audit trail. Compliant processes are treated on par with face-to-face CIP.
Several individual wire transfers sent to the same financial institutions, which may or may not be ultimately intended for different persons.
Natural or legal person or legal arrangement that the originator identifies as the receiver of the requested wire transfer.
RBI-regulated financial institution that receives the wire transfer from the ordering financial institution, directly or via an intermediary RE, and makes funds available to the beneficiary.

Wire transfer combining a payment message sent directly from the ordering financial institution to the beneficiary financial institution with the funding instruction (cover) routed through one or more intermediary financial institutions.
Any wire transfer where the ordering and beneficiary financial institutions are in different countries, including any chain in which at least one institution is in a different country.
Any wire transfer where the ordering and beneficiary financial institutions are both in India, including chains entirely within India even if the payment system is located in another country.
Same meaning as in the FATF Recommendations, as revised from time to time.

RBI-regulated financial institution handling an intermediary element of a serial or cover payment chain, receiving and transmitting the wire transfer on behalf of the ordering or beneficiary financial institution or another intermediary.
RBI-regulated financial institution that initiates the wire transfer and transfers funds on receiving the request on behalf of the originator.
Account holder who allows the wire transfer from the account or, where there is no account, the natural or legal person placing the order with the ordering financial institution.

Direct sequential payment chain in which the wire transfer and accompanying payment message travel together from the ordering to the beneficiary financial institution, directly or via intermediaries such as correspondent banks.
Payment transactions conducted electronically without the need for manual intervention.
Combination of letters, numbers or symbols determined by the payment service provider under the protocols of the payment and settlement or messaging system used.

Any transaction carried out on behalf of an originator through a financial institution by electronic means to make funds available to a beneficiary at a beneficiary financial institution, whether or not originator and beneficiary are the same person.

MD-MFI.def: A company registered under section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, or the corresponding provision of the Companies Act, 2013.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
A non-deposit taking NBFC which has a minimum of 60 percent of its total assets (netted off by intangible assets) deployed towards microfinance loans on an ongoing basis.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025.
The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act 2 of 1934).
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 (same elements as prescribed there).
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 (same elements as prescribed there).

MD-MFI.term: Words or expressions not defined herein
MD-MFI.def: Same meaning as in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 or the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; any other word not defined in those Acts takes its meaning from the Companies Act, 1956 or the Companies Act, 2013.

Aligned with microfinance loans (para 8(2)). Must be at least 60 percent of total assets (netted off by intangible assets) on an ongoing basis. If not maintained for four consecutive quarters, the NBFC-MFI must approach the Reserve Bank with a remediation plan.
An asset in respect of which no default in repayment of principal or payment of interest is perceived, which discloses no problem, and which carries no more than normal risk attached to the business.
MD-MFI.scope: Asset classification norms for microfinance loans (para 22, B.1)

MD-MFI.def: An asset for which interest or principal payment has remained overdue for a period of more than 90 days.
MD-MFI.scope: Asset classification norms for microfinance loans (para 22, B.1)

MD-MGC.def: Banking company; corresponding new bank; State Bank of India; subsidiary bank; any bank RBI notifies for these guidelines; or co-operative bank under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Same meaning as in Section 5(c) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Any person or entity granted a housing loan by a creditor institution or other entity RBI specifies.
Equity capital and reserves less intangible assets and revaluation reserves, divided by the investee's number of equity shares.
Book value of assets plus interest accrued but not received.
Company registered under Section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, or corresponding provision of the Companies Act, 2013.
Same meaning as in clause (da) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
A bank or a housing finance company.
Non-payment on the due date of any principal or interest payable by a borrower to a creditor institution.
Asset that remains a sub-standard asset for a period exceeding 12 months.

Average post-tax profit of the preceding three years, less preference dividend and adjusted for extraordinary and non-recurring items, divided by investee's equity shares, capitalised at 8% (predominantly manufacturing), 10% (predominantly trading) or 12% (any other company, including NBFC). Loss-making investee: zero.
Mean of earning value and breakup value.
Same meaning as in section 126 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Housing Finance Companies) Directions, 2025.

Loan or advance to an individual or other RBI-specified entity (including housing societies and co-operatives) for construction, repairs, upgradation or acquisition of a house or residential property, or both.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025.

(i) Asset identified as loss by the MGC, its internal or external auditor, or RBI, to the extent not written off; (ii) asset adversely affected by a potential threat of non-recoverability, such as erosion or non-availability of security, or fraud by the borrower.
Guarantee by an MGC for repayment of an outstanding housing loan and accrued interest, up to the guaranteed amount, to a creditor institution, on a trigger event.
Company registered with RBI as a mortgage guarantee company that primarily transacts mortgage guarantee business.
Tri-partite contract among the borrower, the creditor institution and the MGC, which provides the mortgage guarantee.
National Housing Bank established under the National Housing Bank Act, 1987 (53 of 1987).

Paid-up equity capital and free reserves per latest balance sheet, less accumulated losses, deferred revenue expenditure and other intangibles; further reduced by investments in shares of subsidiaries, same-group companies and other NBFCs, and by book value of debentures, bonds, loans and deposits with subsidiaries or same-group companies exceeding 10% of that base.

Account classified by a creditor institution as sub-standard, doubtful or loss under RBI asset classification directions. MG assets acquired on a trigger event are NPA immediately. For income recognition on MGC investments, NPA means interest or principal overdue for more than 90 days.
Latest declared net asset value by the mutual fund for that particular scheme.

Paid-up equity, free reserves incl. quarterly profits, contingency reserves (paras 43-50), share premium, and asset-sale capital reserves; excludes revaluation reserves. Less accumulated losses, intangibles, deferred revenue expenditure. Quarterly profits count only with quarterly limited review/audit, net of 0.25 x average three-year dividend. Current-year losses fully deducted. No ROU asset deduction if the leased asset is tangible.
Reserve Bank of India constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934).
Asset with no perceived default in principal or interest, no visible problem, and no more than normal business risk.

MD-MGC.term: sub-standard asset in respect of mortgage guarantee asset
MD-MGC.def: Asset classified as NPA for a period not exceeding 12 months.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025; capital treatment also per those Directions.

Beneficial interest held by an individual, spouse or minor child, singly or together, in a company's shares exceeding 10% of its paid-up capital; or capital subscribed by all partners of a partnership firm.

Owned fund less investments in shares of other NBFCs, and in shares, debentures, bonds, loans, advances (incl. hire purchase and lease finance) and deposits with subsidiaries or same-group companies, where the aggregate exceeds 10% of owned fund. Applies to holdings acquired in satisfaction of debt.

(i) Preference shares; (ii) revaluation reserves at 55% discounted rate; (iii) general provisions and loss reserves not attributable to identified diminution, plus provisions on standard assets, up to 1.25% of risk-weighted assets; (iv) hybrid debt capital instruments; (v) subordinated debt. Total not to exceed Tier 1 capital.
Classification of a borrower's account as NPA in the books of the creditor institution.
Total mortgage guarantee contracts entered during the year, plus business from other RBI-permitted activities undertaken during the year.

MD-MISC.def: Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Directions, 2025.

MD-MISC.term: Words or expressions not defined herein
MD-MISC.def: Same meaning as in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 or the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; any other word not defined in those Acts takes its meaning from the Companies Act, 1956 or the Companies Act, 2013.

MD-NOFHC.def: Capital, Reserves and Surplus of the NOFHC determined on consolidation of its subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures in accordance with the applicable Accounting Standards.

A non-deposit taking NBFC which holds the shares of a banking company and the shares of all other financial services companies in its group (whether regulated by RBI or any other financial regulator), to the extent permissible under applicable regulatory prescriptions.

A person who, together with relatives (as defined in section 2(77) of the Companies Act, 2013 and its Rules), by virtue of ownership of voting equity shares, is or will be in effective control of the bank or NOFHC; includes, where applicable, all entities in the Promoter Group.
Any arrangement, whether in the form of shareholding, agreement or otherwise, which enables exercise of control.
The entity that promotes the bank.

Promoter and relatives. Corporate promoter: holding/subsidiary entities; bodies corporate with 10%+ holding either way, or where a group holding 20%+ also holds 20%+ of promoter; JVs, associates, related parties. Individual promoter: bodies corporate with 10%+ held by promoter/relatives; HUFs/firms with 10%+ aggregate holding. AoA-declared promoters and common-brand entities. FIs, FIIs, mutual funds holding 10%+ of promoter excluded unless strategic.
As defined under Accounting Standards Ind AS 110 and Ind AS 28.
Of the promoter group: dealings constituting 10% or more of annual purchases or sales, or both taken together.
Debt instruments which RBI has treated as capital of the issuing entity for capital adequacy purposes.
Entities which are outside the scope of regulatory consolidation.

MD-NOFHC.term: Consolidated capital funds for regulatory purpose
MD-NOFHC.def: The consolidated regulatory capital of the NOFHC under the regulatory scope of consolidation, per the Commercial Banks Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy and Financial Statements: Presentation and Disclosures Directions, 2025.

MD-OUTS.def: Use of a third party (an affiliated group entity or an external entity) by an NBFC to perform, on a continuing basis, activities normally undertaken by the NBFC itself, now or in future. Continuing basis includes agreements for a limited period.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Concentration Risk Management) Directions, 2025, as amended.
Arrangements which, if disrupted, have the potential to significantly impact business operations, reputation, profitability or customer service.
MD-OUTS.scope: Chapter III (outsourcing of financial services) only

MD-OUTS.def: Based on: importance of the activity and the risk it poses; impact on earnings, solvency, liquidity, funding, capital and risk profile; impact on reputation, brand and ability to meet objectives if provider fails; cost as a share of total operating costs; aggregate exposure to the same provider; and significance for customer service and protection.
MD-OUTS.scope: Chapter III (outsourcing of financial services) only

MD-OUTS.def: Banking companies (other than Small Finance Banks, LABs, Payments Banks and RRBs), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined under clauses (c), (da) and (nc) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

Indicative, non-exhaustive list: Commercial Banks; LABs; Small Finance Banks; Payments Banks; RRBs; NBFCs in Base, Middle and Upper Layer; AIFIs; Credit Information Companies; Urban Co-operative Banks; Rural Co-operative Banks; and Payment System Operators.
MD-OUTS.scope: Used for the corporate internet banking exclusion in para 5(2)(i)

MD-P2P.def: A company as defined in clause (20) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Total Outside Liabilities divided by Owned Funds, of the NBFC-P2P.
A loan where interest and/or instalment of principal remains overdue for a period of more than 90 days.
A person who has entered into an arrangement with an NBFC-P2P to lend on it or to avail of loan facilitation services provided by it.
Includes an individual, a body of individuals, a HUF, a firm, a society, or any artificial body, whether incorporated or not.
An intermediary providing loan facilitation services, via online medium or otherwise, to the participants defined in para 7(4).

A non-banking institution carrying on the business of a Peer to Peer Lending Platform. Explanation: electronic platforms acting as DSA/business correspondents only for banks, NBFCs or regulated AIFIs (to identify borrowers) are not P2P platforms; if other retail lenders also use the platform, it must register separately as an NBFC-P2P. An existing NBFC cannot operate as an NBFC-P2P.

MD-P2P.term: Words or expressions not defined herein
MD-P2P.def: Same meaning as in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 or the Companies Act, 2013.

Capital infused in the business plus surplus generated out of the NBFC-P2P's business. Excludes lenders' and borrowers' funds flowing through escrow accounts; customers' funds lent or borrowed via the platform cannot be used by the platform.
MD-P2P.scope: Only the proviso to para 24 (deployment in RBI-specified instruments, not for trading)

MD-P2P.def: T is the date funds are received in the escrow accounts; funds must not remain there beyond T+1, where T+1 is the next bank working day.
MD-P2P.scope: Lenders' and Borrowers' escrow accounts only

MD-PA.def: Merchant transaction in which banknotes or currency notes (legal tender in India) are offered or tendered at the time of delivery of goods and/or services.
Physical verification of the address or place of business of the merchant.

Buying and selling of goods and services, including digital products, over digital and electronic networks. The network includes computers, television channels and other automated internet applications such as web pages, extranets and mobiles.
Transaction involving an inflow of foreign exchange.
E-commerce entity providing an IT platform on a digital or electronic network to facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers.
Entity or marketplace that sells goods, provides services, or offers investment products; includes exporters and overseas sellers.
Transaction involving an outflow of foreign exchange.
Method or manner through which a payment instruction is initiated and processed in a payment system.

Entity that aggregates customers' payments to merchants through one or more payment channels, via the merchant's physical or virtual interface, for goods, services or investment products, and then settles the collected funds to those merchants. Categories: PA-P, PA-CB and PA-O.
PA facilitating transactions where the acceptance device and payment instrument are physically present in close proximity at the time of the transaction.

PA facilitating cross-border payments for current account transactions not prohibited under FEMA, for onboarded merchants via e-commerce; sub-types: inward and outward. Excludes non-bank AD Category-II entities doing current account transactions other than purchase or sale of goods/services, and card transactions where a card network facilitates foreign exchange settlement and the aggregator receives local currency.
PA facilitating transactions where the acceptance device and payment instrument are not present in close proximity while making the transaction.
Entity providing technology infrastructure to route and facilitate processing of payment transactions, without any involvement in handling funds.
MD-PA.scope: Not within the scope of this MD (see para 10g)

MD-PA.term: CKYCR, OVD, equivalent e-document, digital KYC, V-CIP
MD-PA.def: Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (DOR.AML.REC.No.88/14.01.002/2025-26), as amended.

MD-PA.term: Inward Collection Account (InCA) and Outward Collection Account (OCA)
MD-PA.def: Non-bank PA escrow accounts for merchant funds must be with a Scheduled Commercial Bank in India. For a PA-CB, the account is also called InCA (for inward transactions) or OCA (for outward transactions), as applicable.

MD-PPI.def: PPIs issued by an entity for purchase of goods and services from that entity only, not permitting cash withdrawal and not usable for third-party payment or settlement. Not classified as a payment system requiring RBI approval/authorisation, so not regulated or supervised by RBI.
Banks and non-banks that have RBI approval/authorisation to issue PPIs, and those proposing to issue PPIs.
Individuals or organisations that obtain or purchase PPIs from the issuer and use them for purchase of goods and services, financial services, remittance facilities, etc.
Entities issuing PPIs to individuals or organisations.
All value limits stated in this MD are the maximum INR value of instruments that may be issued.
Establishments with a specific contract to accept the issuer's PPIs (directly, or through a payment aggregator or payment gateway) against sale of goods and services, financial services, etc.

Paid-up equity capital, compulsorily convertible preference shares, free reserves, share premium and capital reserves from asset-sale surplus (excluding revaluation reserves), less accumulated losses, intangible assets and deferred revenue expenditure. Compulsorily convertible preference shares may be cumulative or non-cumulative, but must convert into equity and shareholder agreements must bar withdrawal at any time.

Instruments that facilitate purchase of goods and services, financial services, remittance facilities, etc., against the value stored in them. Those needing RBI approval/authorisation before issue are of two types: Small PPIs and Full-KYC PPIs.

Issued by banks and non-banks after obtaining minimum details of the holder. Only for purchase of goods and services; no funds transfer or cash withdrawal. Usable at identified merchant locations with a specific contract with the issuer (directly or via a payment aggregator or payment gateway). Features in para 9.1.
Issued by banks and non-banks after completing KYC of the holder. Usable for purchase of goods and services, funds transfer and cash withdrawal. Features in para 9.2.

MD-PSL.def: Activities allied to agriculture, including dairy, fisheries, animal husbandry, poultry, bee-keeping, sericulture and similar activities.

Individual farmers, including small and marginal farmers (SMFs); proprietorship firms of farmers directly engaged in agriculture and allied activities; and self-help groups (SHGs) or joint liability groups (JLGs) of individual farmers. Groups qualify only if banks maintain disaggregated data of such loans.

Loans sanctioned by banks to eligible intermediaries for onward lending. Such loans are eligible for PSL classification only if extended for creating priority sector assets and those assets remain deployed.

MD-RBC.def: Annual cost of credit to the borrower, including the interest rate and all other charges associated with the credit facility.
Same meaning as in XBRL Returns - Harmonization of Banking Statistics dated January 04, 2018, as amended from time to time.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Equated or fixed amount of principal and interest repayments paid by a borrower at periodic intervals for a fixed number of intervals, resulting in complete amortisation of the loan.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Legally significant and deterministic facts that satisfy the basic information needed to help the borrower take an informed financial decision.
Statement of key facts of a loan agreement, in simple, easy-to-understand language, provided to the borrower in a standardised format.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Microfinance Institution) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in XBRL Returns - Harmonization of Banking Statistics dated January 04, 2018, as amended from time to time.
MD-RBC.scope: Paragraphs under Sections D and F of Chapter III only

MD-RBC.def: For this Direction: (i) Scheduled Commercial Banks, RRBs, LABs, primary UCBs, StCBs/CCBs, Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks and any entity licensed under section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; (ii) AIFIs; (iii) NBFCs and Housing Finance Companies.
MD-RBC.scope: Limited purpose of this Direction only

MD-RBC.def: Period available to the borrower, after being provided the KFS, to agree to the loan terms. If the borrower agrees within this period, the NBFC is bound by the loan terms indicated in the KFS.
MD-RBC.scope: Key Facts Statement provisions in para 29 only

MD-RETURNS.def: An online platform of RBI for return submission, data dissemination and other related purposes.
All periodic and ad-hoc data submitted to RBI in prescribed formats, irrespective of technology platform, periodicity or mode of submission.

MD-SA.def: NBFCs (including Housing Finance Companies) as defined in the RBI (NBFC - Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Directions, 2025.
MD-SA.scope: Appointment / reappointment of SCAs / SAs only; non-deposit taking NBFCs with asset size below Rs 1,000 crore may continue their extant procedure

MD-SA.def: The term SCAs applies to NBFCs that appoint separate Statutory Branch Auditors (SBAs); in all other cases the term SAs applies.
NABARD, SIDBI, National Housing Bank, EXIM Bank and NaBFID, as established under their respective statutes.
A partnership firm or a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP).
Same meaning as in Sub-section (d) of Section 2 of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981.

Banking companies (including Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks and State Bank of India, as defined in clauses (c), (da) and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

Two or more entities related through: subsidiary-parent (AS 21); joint venture (AS 27); associate (AS 23); promoter-promotee for listed companies (SEBI Acquisition of Shares and Takeover Regulations, 1997); related party (AS 18); common brand name; or investment in equity shares of 20 per cent and above.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC - Concentration Risk Management) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in Section 5(ccv) read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
State Bank of India and corresponding new banks, collectively.
Same meaning as in Section 5(nc) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Same meaning as in Sub-section (u) of Section 2 of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981.
In these paragraphs, Group Entities means RBI-regulated entities in the group that fulfil the para 4(5) definition.

For NBFCs above Rs 1,000 crore, the full-time partner must not be a partner in another audit firm, must not be employed full or part time elsewhere, and must not practise in own name or otherwise under Section 2(2) of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. Board/ACB must ensure firm income makes the association exclusive. Requires at least one year's continuous association as on shortlisting date.
MD-SA.scope: Eligibility criteria table (Chapter III B) only

MD-SA.def: Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) or Information Systems Audit (ISA) qualification. For Paid CAs, requires at least one year's continuous association with the firm as on shortlisting date. No minimum for NBFCs up to Rs 1,000 crore.
MD-SA.scope: Eligibility criteria table (Chapter III B) only

MD-SA.def: Experience as Statutory Central or Branch Auditor of Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, Local Area Banks, AIFIs, UCBs and NBFCs. On merger of audit firms, merger effect is given after two years; demerger is effective immediately.
MD-SA.scope: Eligibility criteria table (Chapter III B) only

MD-SA.def: Audit and article clerks with book-keeping knowledge who are engaged in on-site audits; excludes typists, stenographers, computer operators, secretaries and subordinate staff. Requires at least one year's continuous association with the firm as on shortlisting date.
MD-SA.scope: Eligibility criteria table (Chapter III B) only

MD-SA.term: Group of audit firms (common partners or same network)
MD-SA.def: Audit firms with common partners and/or under the same network are treated as one entity for allotment of SCAs/SAs. Shared or sub-contracted audit by an associate firm in the same network is not permissible.

MD-SBR.def: Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Core Investment Companies) Directions, 2025.
A company registered under section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, or the corresponding provision under the Companies Act, 2013.

Two or more entities related by: subsidiary-parent (AS 21); joint venture (AS 27); associate (AS 23); promoter-promotee (SEBI Acquisition of Shares and Takeover Regulations, 1997, for listed companies); related party (AS 18); common brand name; or investment in equity shares of 20 per cent and above.
MD-SBR.scope: Only for determining applicability of prudential norms on multiple NBFCs in a group (Explanation to para 6(3)).

MD-SBR.def: Interaction between the NBFC and its customers while carrying on its business.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Housing Finance Companies) Directions, 2025.

A non-deposit taking NBFC permitted to: (i) refinance post-COD infrastructure projects that have completed at least one year of satisfactory commercial operations; and (ii) finance toll operate transfer (TOT) projects as the direct lender.

Credit facility by an NBFC to a borrower: term loan, project loan, subscription to bonds, debentures, preference or equity shares in a project company acquired as part of a project finance package (subscription must be in the nature of advance), or other long-term funded facility, for exposure in infrastructure sub-sectors notified by Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, from time to time.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Mortgage Guarantee Companies) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as Account Aggregator in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Account Aggregator) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as Deposit taking NBFC in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Acceptance of Public Deposits) Directions, 2025.

NBFC as defined in clause (f) of section 45-I of the RBI Act, 1934, whose principal business is as specified in the Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, and which holds a certificate of registration under section 3 of the Factoring Regulation Act, 2011.

Company that is a financial institution whose principal business is asset finance, or providing finance by loans, advances or otherwise for any activity other than its own, or acquisition of securities; and is not any other NBFC category defined in an RBI Master Direction.
Non-deposit taking NBFC which has a minimum of 75 per cent of its total assets deployed towards infrastructure lending.
Same meaning as NBFC-MFI in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Microfinance Institution) Directions, 2025.

MD-SBR.term: NBFC not availing public funds and not having any customer interface
MD-SBR.def: NBFC registered as Type I NBFC or otherwise that: (i) does not accept, and does not intend to accept in future, public funds; and (ii) has no customer interface and does not intend to have one in future. Explanation: public funds and customer interface have the meanings given in these Directions.
Same meaning as Non-Banking Financial Company - Peer to Peer Lending Platform in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Peer to Peer Lending Platform) Directions, 2025.

Non-deposit taking NBFC referred to in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Operating Financial Holding Companies) Directions, 2025, which holds shares of a banking company and of all other financial services companies in its group (whether regulated by RBI or another financial regulator), to the extent permissible under applicable prescriptions.
Same meaning as in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Acceptance of Public Deposits) Directions, 2025.

Funds raised directly or indirectly through public deposits, inter-corporate deposits, bank finance and all funds from outside sources such as commercial papers or debentures. Excludes funds raised by instruments compulsorily convertible into equity shares within a period not exceeding five years from date of issue.
Funds received not directly but through associates and Group entities which have access to public funds.
The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act 2 of 1934).
The Reserve Bank of India constituted under section 3 of the RBI Act, 1934.
Company registered as NBFC under section 45-IA of the RBI Act, 1934 and authorised by RBI to undertake Primary Dealer (PD) activity.
NBFC not availing public funds and not having any customer interface, as defined in these Directions, and holding a Certificate of Registration as Type I NBFC issued by RBI.
NBFC granted a Certificate of Registration by RBI as an NBFC other than Type I NBFC.
NBFC not availing public funds and not having any customer interface, as defined in these Directions, and exempted from sections 45IA and 45IC of the RBI Act, 1934 as detailed in para 65A.

MD-SEC.def: Unlikelihood that an entity becomes subject to voluntary or involuntary bankruptcy proceedings, including by the originator or its creditors.

Option letting the originator call the underlying or securitisation exposures when their outstanding value falls below a pre-defined threshold, extinguishing all parties' remaining securitisation exposures.
Contractual arrangement where an entity mitigates credit risk of a securitisation exposure by providing added protection to other transaction parties.
Mechanism which, once triggered, accelerates reduction of investors' interest in the underlying exposures and allows investors to be paid before the stated maturity of the notes.
Difference between gross finance charge collections and other SPE income, and securitisation notes interest, servicing fees, charge-offs and other senior SPE expenses.
For a securitisation exposure: on-balance sheet amount or carrying value (after purchase discounts and write-downs or specific provisions), plus off-balance sheet exposure amount where applicable.
First level of financial support by the originator or a third party improving the creditworthiness of SPE notes, so the provider bears part or all of the risks of the SPE's assets.
Protection arising when an NBFC supports a securitisation in excess of its predetermined contractual obligation.
On-balance sheet originator asset representing valuation of cash flows from future margin income. If subordinated, it is a credit-enhancing interest-only strip.

Unless specifically stated otherwise: scheduled commercial banks (excluding regional rural banks); AIFIs (NABARD, NHB, EXIM Bank, SIDBI); small finance banks as permitted under the SFB Securitisation Directions, 2025; and all NBFCs including HFCs.
Securitisation notes issued by the SPE against underlying exposures all secured by commercial or residential real estate mortgages.

Lender transferring from its balance sheet a single asset or pool of assets to an SPE in a securitisation, including other entities of its consolidated group. Need not be the lender that originally sanctioned the loans.
Credit enhancement where underlying exposures are posted at a value higher than the value of the securitisation notes.

Using securitised asset cash flows to acquire more assets, as disclosed upfront, during a pre-announced replenishment period, after which the structure becomes amortising. Assets must be bought from the same originator(s).
Securitisation notes issued by the SPE against underlying exposures all secured by residential mortgages.
Securitisation exposure where at least one underlying exposure is itself a securitisation exposure.
For these Directions, exposures not classified as non-performing assets.

Second or subsequent tier of protection for losses not covered by the first loss facility. Invoked only after the first loss facility is drawn and repudiated or exhausted, or its provider is in insolvency, bankruptcy or liquidation.

Structure where an originator transfers a pool of assets to an SPE and the pool's cash flow services securitisation exposures of at least two tranches of different credit risk; investor payments depend on the underlying performance. A single-asset pool and tranches with different maturities are permitted.

Includes, but not restricted to, exposures to securitisation notes (including ABS and MBS), credit enhancements, underwriting commitments, liquidity facilities, interest rate or currency swaps, credit derivatives and tranched cover. Reserve accounts recorded as originator assets, such as cash collateral accounts, are included.
Securities issued by the SPE as part of a securitisation.

Tranche with a first claim on the entire amount of the underlying pool. If all tranches above the first-loss piece are rated, the most highly rated is senior. Among equal ratings only the most senior in the cash flow waterfall is senior, unless the only difference is maturity, in which case all are senior.

Company, trust or other entity organised for a specific purpose, limited to that purpose, and structured to isolate it from the originator's credit risk. Any reference to an SPE also covers a trust settled as part of the securitisation.
Any tranche junior to the senior tranche(s).

Structure where credit risk of an underlying pool is transferred, wholly or partly, through credit derivatives or guarantees hedging credit risk that remains on the NBFC's balance sheet. Excludes instruments permitted to NBFCs for hedging under current instructions.

Contractual segment of the credit risk of an exposure or pool, where a position carries greater or lesser credit loss risk than an equal position in another segment, ignoring third-party protection to holders. Securitisation notes and credit enhancement facilities are treated as tranches.

MD-SPD.def: Risk that a transaction counterparty defaults before the transaction's cash flows are finally settled. It is bilateral, since the market value of the transaction can be positive or negative for either party.

Transactions with one counterparty under a legally enforceable bilateral netting arrangement recognised for capital purposes. A transaction without such an arrangement is its own netting set. Cross-product netting of OTC derivatives with repo/reverse repo is not permitted.
Repurchase and reverse repurchase agreements, securities lending and borrowing, and CBLO, where value depends on market valuations and transactions are often subject to margin agreements.

Fully paid-up, unsecured, subordinate, restriction-free instrument not redeemable at holder's initiative or without RBI consent. Excluded from Tier 2 if initial maturity under 5 years or remaining maturity under 1 year; Tier 2 SD capped at 50% of Tier 1. Discount by residual maturity: under 1y 100%, 1-2y 80%, 2-3y 60%, 3-4y 40%, 4-5y 20%.

Paid-up capital, statutory reserves and disclosed free reserves, incl. quarterly profits (only with quarterly limited review/audit, net of 0.25 x average three-year dividend). Deducted: current-year losses, subsidiary investments (where applicable), intangibles, deferred tax assets, brought-forward losses, and substantial non-business loans to group companies. ROU assets not deducted if leased asset is tangible.

(i) Undisclosed reserves and cumulative preference shares (not compulsorily convertible), fully paid and without holder-redemption clauses; (ii) revaluation reserves discounted at 55%; (iii) general provisions and loss reserves, up to 1.25% of total risk-weighted assets; (iv) hybrid debt instruments; (v) subordinated debt.

MD-STRESS.def: All fund-based and non-fund-based exposure, including investment exposure.
Negotiated arrangement with the borrower to fully settle the NBFC's claims in cash. It may involve a sacrifice of the amount due, with a corresponding waiver of claims.

For projects under implementation, triggered by any of: (i) default with any lender; (ii) lenders determine need to extend original or extended DCCO; (iii) expiry of original or extended DCCO; (iv) lenders determine need for additional debt infusion; (v) project in financial difficulty under paras 13 to 15.
For Chapter VI-A: date on which the borrower and NBFC agree, through a documented arrangement, to proceed with a resolution plan, other than a deemed invocation under para 122J.
Non-payment of debt (as defined under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016) when any part or instalment has become due and payable and is not paid by the debtor or corporate debtor.
Interest accrued on debt provided by an NBFC and capitalised during the construction phase of the project.
(i) Commercial banks, including SFBs but excluding PBs, LABs and RRBs; (ii) NBFCs, including HFCs; (iii) Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks; (iv) All India Financial Institutions.
Estimated realisable value of the borrower's assets if liquidated on the date the Review Period commences.
Period from implementation of the resolution plan until at least 10% of the outstanding principal debt under the plan, plus any interest capitalisation sanctioned in restructuring, is repaid.
Event recognised under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) or State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF).

All credit facilities, including debt and debt-like instruments (e.g. NCDs, optionally convertible debentures and preference shares, non-convertible preference shares), existing after the resolution plan is implemented. Only equity and instruments compulsorily convertible into equity, without embedded optionality, are exempt.
Aggregate outstanding principal debt to be held by all specified lenders under the proposed resolution plan.

For projects under implementation: a mutually agreed, legally binding, feasible, time-bound plan to resolve stress in a project finance account, which may include payment of overdues, sale of exposures, change in ownership, DCCO extension and restructuring.

Concession granted by an NBFC, for economic or legal reasons tied to the borrower's financial difficulty, e.g. changing payment period, amount, instalments or interest rate; rolling over facilities; sanctioning additional credit to cure default; enhancing limits. Compromise settlements count where settlement payment time exceeds three months.
30 days from the date of default or credit event, as the case may be.
Borrower is not in default with any specified lender at any point during the period concerned.

(i) Commercial banks, including SFBs but excluding PBs, LABs and RRBs; (ii) All India Financial Institutions; (iii) deposit-taking NBFCs, excluding HFCs; (iv) non-deposit-taking NBFCs, excluding HFCs, with asset size of ₹500 crore and above.
Immovable asset acquired by an NBFC in satisfaction or part satisfaction of its claims on the borrower.

Period from implementation of the resolution plan until at least 20% of the outstanding principal debt under the plan, plus sanctioned interest capitalisation, is repaid. For IBC-restructured accounts, it starts from implementation as approved by the Adjudicating Authority.
Contingent credit line sanctioned at financial closure to fund cost overruns during the project's construction phase.
NPAs kept outstanding at borrower account level but written off, fully or partly, only for accounting purposes, without waiving claims and without prejudice to recovery.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.

MD-STRESS.term: Original Date of Commencement of Commercial Operations (Original DCCO)
MD-STRESS.def: Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.

MD-SUPMISC.def: Defined in the RBI (NBFC - Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Directions, 2025, which this page does not reproduce. Used to exclude NBFCs not accepting or not intending to accept public funds from Chapter V.

Solution akin to banks' Core Banking Solution: seamless customer interface for digital offerings, integration of NBFC functions, centralised database and accounting records, and MIS for internal and regulatory use. Mandatory for Upper and Middle Layer NBFCs with 10 and more fixed point service delivery units.

A place of operation from which the NBFC carries on non-banking financial intermediation, manned by its own or outsourced staff, with uniform signage bearing the NBFC's name and under its administrative control. Administrative and back offices with no direct customer interface are excluded.

MD-TDCR.def: Contractual arrangement where an entity gives added protection to other parties to a transaction to mitigate credit risk of their acquired exposures.
Non-payment of debt (as defined under the IBC, 2016) when any part or instalment has become due and payable and is not paid by the debtor or corporate debtor.
Risks and rewards that may arise from a loan exposure through its life.

Scheduled commercial banks; regional rural banks; local area banks; primary (urban), state and central co-operative banks; AIFIs (NABARD, NHB, EXIM, SIDBI, NaBFID); small finance banks; NBFCs including HFCs. Regional rural banks, local area banks and primary, state and central co-operative banks may be transferors of stressed loans only, under Chapter IV of Part A.

Transfer of all or part of economic interest in a loan without transferring the loan contract; transferee funds transferor to the extent transferred. Only by contractual agreement; transferor remains lender of record; transferee's exposure is to the underlying borrower, not the transferor.
Minimum period for which a transferor must hold loan exposures before transferring them.
Funded outstanding in a loan exposure, reduced by specific provisions made against it.
Scheduled commercial banks; All India Financial Companies (NABARD, NHB, EXIM, SIDBI, NaBFID); small finance banks; and NBFCs including HFCs.

Loans to individuals: (a) consumer credit, (b) education loans, (c) loans to create or enhance immovable assets (e.g. housing), (d) loans for investment in financial assets (shares, debentures). A loan within this definition is a personal loan even if not so classified in reporting.
Set of loan exposures transferred together at one point of time under the same transfer agreement. The agreement must list the individual loan exposures.
Loan exposures classified as non-performing assets (NPA) or special mention accounts (SMA).

Point when the associated risks and rewards, to the extent of economic interest transferred and as documented in the participation, assignment or novation contract, become binding on transferor and transferee.
Transfer of economic interest in loan exposures to transferee(s), with or without transfer of the loan contract, as permitted under Part A. The transferee thereby acquires the loan exposures.

Entity receiving economic interest in a loan under Part A. Must not be disqualified under Section 29A of the IBC, 2016. Where fraud is detected in a borrower's accounts, transferee must not belong to the borrower's existing promoter group, nor be its subsidiary, associate or related party. Transferor must verify compliance.

MD-TDCR.term: promoter group and related party (for transferee provisos)
MD-TDCR.def: 'Promoter group' has the same meaning as in SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018; 'related party' has the same meaning as in the IBC, 2016.
Entity which transfers economic interest in a loan exposure under these Directions.

MD-WD.def: One who has availed a credit facility from an NBFC.

Any fund-based or non-fund-based facility, including off-balance sheet items such as derivatives, guarantees and letters of credit, extended by an NBFC to a borrower (without prejudice to the non-fund-based provisions of the Credit Facilities Directions, 2025).
Company granted a certificate of registration under Section 5 of the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Resolution of Stressed Assets) Directions, 2025.
Director of a company classified as a large or wilful defaulter who was associated with the company when the acts of omission or commission leading to the default occurred.
Same meaning as in the Companies Act, 2013.

Includes: short-term working capital used for long-term purposes contrary to sanction terms; funds used for assets other than those sanctioned; transfers to group or other entities, or investments in them, without NBFC or all-consortium approval; routing funds via other lenders without written permission; unaccounted shortfall in deployment.
Person or entity who has guaranteed the credit facility.

Committee an NBFC constitutes to identify a wilful defaulter: chaired by an officer not more than one rank below the MD/CEO, with two senior officials not more than two ranks below the chairperson as members.
Same meaning as in the Companies Act, 2013.
Defaulter with outstanding amount of ₹1 crore and above, where either (a) a suit has been filed, or (b) the account is classified doubtful or loss under RBI instructions.

Entity that has granted the borrower a credit facility: (a) commercial banks, including SFBs, RRBs and LABs but excluding Payments Banks; (b) Scheduled Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks; (c) non-scheduled Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks in Tier 3 and 4; (d) All India Financial Institutions (EXIM, NABARD, NHB, SIDBI, NaBFID); (e) NBFCs in NBFC-ML and above layers.
Director nominated by a lender, a regulatory authority, or the Central or a State Government.

Person named as such in a prospectus or identified in the annual return who (a) controls the company's affairs directly or indirectly, as shareholder, director or otherwise, and/or (b) whose advice, directions or instructions the Board is accustomed to act on.

Committee an NBFC constitutes to review the Identification Committee's proposal, chaired by the MD/CEO with two independent or non-executive directors (or equivalent officials) as members. Identification Committee members cannot sit on it.
Occurs if funds availed through a credit facility from an NBFC are used for purposes unrelated to the borrower's operations.

Account where an RBI-regulated entity has approached a court or tribunal (including under IBC, 2016) for recovery and proceedings are pending; includes pending applications, appeals or execution in continuation of recovery, and SARFAESI or other recovery or resolution or liquidation proceedings still continuing.

Deemed where the borrower defaults on payment obligations to the lender and one or more of these is noticed: (a) capacity to honour obligations; (b) diverted credit funds; (c) siphoned funds; (d) disposed of secured assets without lender approval; (e) borrower or promoter failed to infuse committed equity despite ability, although lender gave loans or concessions relying on that commitment.

Deemed where a guarantor does not honour an invoked guarantee despite sufficient means, or disposes of secured assets without lender approval, or fails a committed equity infusion despite ability, where the lender relied on that commitment.

(a) A borrower or guarantor who committed wilful default with outstanding of ₹25 lakh and above, or as RBI notifies; (b) if a company, its promoters and directors, subject to para 5(14); (c) if another entity, persons in charge of and responsible for its management.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Transfer and Distribution of Credit Risk) Directions, 2025.
Same meaning as in the RBI (NBFC – Transfer and Distribution of Credit Risk) Directions, 2025.
